title: Scientific Models and Computer Tiers: A Unified Theory of Admissibility of Machine-Based Expert Evidence
affiliations: and

detail.title: Scientific Models and Computer Tiers: A Unified Theory of Admissibility of Machine-Based Expert Evidence
detail.abstract: Over the last few decades, researchers have challenged many routinely admissible types of evidence of a suspect’s guilt or innocence (including analysis of bite marks, blood spatter, hair, shoe prints, and toolmarks) and found them lacking in foundational validity. Such methods were initially deemed revolutionary—providing new and more accurate methods of establishing guilt and innocence. Yet, their introduction likely caused many innocent persons to be found guilty and many guilty persons to be found innocent. The introduction of evidence from complex machinebased systems (including artificial intelligence (AI) computer programs) poses a similar challenge. It is one that is poised to provide more accurate ways of establishing guilt and innocence. And it is one that leads us down the same primrose path as bite marks, blood spatter, and hair analysis—to many innocents being found guilty and many of the guilty being found innocent. To help avoid the possibility of AI-based evidence misleading the courts, we propose a three-tiered framework for assessing the admissibility of expert testimony relying on machine-based evidence. Tier One evidence provides no new barriers to admissibility because the machine-based systems underlying it are transparent and explainable. Tier Two evidence arises from proprietary machine-based systems, making those systems only potentially transparent and explainable. As such, courts should admit evidence from Tier Two systems only with access to the underlying system (in the case of AI/computer programs, the code and data) so that it (and opposing counsel) can assess its reliability. Finally, courts should not admit Tier Three evidence, which is based on inherently opaque and unexplainable systems (like many neural networks), because the very structure of the systems creating the evidence makes it impossible for the court to assess its reliability. We contend that due process requires court-ordered disclosure of system architecture and examination by trained experts provided to the accused to ensure proper reliability screening of AI-based evidence prior to admission. Significantly, we find constitutional protections under the Confrontation Clause to be unavailing because, on a practical level, although confrontation rights extend significantly beyond what courts require in the assessment of reliability, confrontation rights must be enforced through a reliability analysis

title: How Do Generative AI Systems Infer Source Trust? An Observational Study of Trust Signalling in AI-Led Information Discovery RESEARCH NOTE

detail.title: How Do Generative AI Systems Infer Source Trust? An Observational Study of Trust Signalling in AI-Led Information Discovery RESEARCH NOTE

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no personal or financial relationships that could be perceived to have influenced the research presented in this paper.

detail.abstract:
This research note presents an independent observational study examining how generative artificial intelligence systems appear to approximate trust when responding to informational queries. Rather than assessing factual accuracy, the study focuses on how trust, credibility, and source reliability are described and inferred in AI-generated responses.

The project involved running sixty repeated, identical prompts across multiple large language models to observe behavioural patterns in AI-led information discovery. Analysis focused on how concepts such as relevance, apparent consensus, repetition across retrieved information, and retrieval structure influence the confidence with which responses are presented, rather than on internal system claims about verification or authority.

The findings suggest that what users experience as trust in generative AI systems typically emerges indirectly through statistical and structural proxies, rather than through explicit assessment of expertise or credibility. The study also identifies meaningful differences in how individual models frame and justify confidence, despite broadly similar underlying behaviour.

The research is published as an observational research note in PDF format and is intended to support understanding of AI visibility, information representation, and the limitations of AI-generated confidence in organisational and decision-making contexts.

title: Cyber Risk Management: A Frameworks, Strategies, and Case Studies in Cybersecurity
affiliations: , University of Johannesburg, Johannesburg, South Africa and University of Johannesburg, Johannesburg, South Africa

detail.title: Cyber Risk Management: A Frameworks, Strategies, and Case Studies in Cybersecurity
detail.abstract: Cyber risk has become a critical concern for organizations as digital transformation accelerates, exposing businesses to increasingly sophisticated and frequent cyber threats. This review examines the frameworks, strategies, and technological solutions used for cyber risk management, focusing on their effectiveness in mitigating risks and enhancing organizational resilience. Covering research published between 2015 and 2025, the findings reveal that widely recognized frameworks such as NIST, ISO 27005, and FAIR are among the most frequently adopted, with a growing shift toward integrating artificial intelligence and predictive analytics to enhance threat detection and response. Despite these advancements, organizations continue to face barriers, including limited resources, a shortage of skilled cybersecurity professionals, and the complexity of implementing comprehensive risk management strategies, especially in small to medium-sized enterprises. Analysis shows that 69% of studies focus on critical infrastructure and financial sectors, reflecting their heightened vulnerability to cyberattacks, while 31% of publications do not specify the frameworks or tools used, indicating a lack of methodological transparency in current research. The review emphasizes the need for adaptable, cost-effective cyber risk management solutions and stronger collaboration between academia, industry, and government to address regulatory complexities and close existing knowledge gaps. Empirical validation of emerging tools and frameworks is crucial to shaping robust and future-ready cybersecurity practices.

title: The Effect of Large Language Models on Audit Quality: Causal Evidence from a Randomized Field Experiment
affiliations: Heinrich Heine University Dusseldorf, , Paderborn University and

detail.title: The Effect of Large Language Models on Audit Quality: Causal Evidence from a Randomized Field Experiment
detail.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly reshaping knowledge-intensive work. Still, evidence on how large language models (LLM) affect performance in regulated, judgment-intensive settings remains limited. We study how access to a firm-specific LLM influences auditor performance using a preregistered randomized field experiment with 100 professional auditors at a global audit firm. Auditors completed a complex inventory valuation task either using the traditional digital tool set or with additional LLM support. We find that access to the firm-specific LLM significantly improves audit output quality and reduces task completion time. Auditors with LLM access produce more formally correct documentation and complete tasks faster, with the largest gains accruing to active users. In contrast, LLM access does not improve adherence to internal audit guidelines, and performance gains do not differ systematically by auditor experience. Both the substantial heterogeneity in LLM adoption and the absence of experience-based differences are surprising, given prior evidence that LLMs benefits less-experienced users. These findings extend research on human-AI collaboration by showing that, in regulated professional work, LLMs enhance productivity and output quality without uniformly strengthening process discipline, revealing important boundary conditions for generative AI at work.

title: Building Equitable Access to Knowledge Through Open Access Repositories
affiliations: Curtin Law School

detail.title: Building Equitable Access to Knowledge Through Open Access Repositories
detail.abstract: This chapter is divided into seven parts. In part one, the background context of the thesis is discussed briefly. The following part articulates the thesis argument and research questions. There is an examination of the theoretical background in part three. Part four briefly analyses regulatory models for OARs. Part five addresses a preliminary literature review and provides justifications for and against OA practices. Part six determines the methodology applied and the last part explains the thesis plan.  This book argues that open access repositories have the potential to provide an equilibrium among the interests of authors, publishers, and users of scientific publications and online published works.

title: Diamond Hard Replication: A Normative Standard for Trustworthy AI‑Assisted Measurement in Social Science
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Diamond Hard Replication: A Normative Standard for Trustworthy AI‑Assisted Measurement in Social Science
detail.abstract:
AI systems are increasingly used to code cases, construct indices, and "read" complex evidence in social science, but fear of hallucination and black-box decision-making undermines trust in their outputs (e.g., Shao, 2025; Wilkinson et al., 2016; MSI Certified, 2023). Existing open-science norms and FAIR data principles improve access and documentation, yet they do not by themselves guarantee that AI-assisted results are computationally reproducible. This paper introduces Diamond Hard replication, a normative standard for AI-assisted research in which, for any given version, a qualified third party can regenerate bit-for-bit identical outputs from documented inputs and scripts and can verify their stability and plausibility through pre-specified audit checks. 
The protocol has five elements: (1) a fixed-seed, time-stamped snapshot that freezes all stochastic steps; (2) a transparent numeric backbone generated exclusively by script from a documented case registry; (3) multi-agent consensus scoring with logged divergences and inter-rater reliability statistics; (4) a small set of anchor cases with published, fixed values for key metrics; and (5) a concise audit checklist that can be implemented as a standing, automated verification process. The paper develops and demonstrates Diamond Hard replication in Archer’s Model of Digital Governance (AMDG), a critical-realist framework applied to a 100+ case library of digital transformation in health, industry, and public administration.
Core indices such as the Digital Skills Maturity Index (DSMI), Action Research Maturity Index (ARMi), and Chaos Resilience Index (CRI) are normalised, checked for internal consistency, and scored by six independent Perplexity Pro agents whose consensus achieves inter-rater reliability ICC 0.94 versus 0.82 for human-only benchmarks. A fixed 25 December 2025 08:06 EET snapshot and np.random.seed(20251225) guarantee deterministic regeneration of the 111-case case-by-metric matrix; five anchor cases (e.g., NHS UK, Hyundai Korea, AgriLedger Ghana) provide ground-truth values that any sceptic can extract with a one-line command and compare to the published table. An external audit checklist requires, at minimum, CSV equality, exact anchor fidelity, and replication of key validity patterns such as the correlation between AMDG and Hofstede PDI and expected Nordic low-PDI/high-ARMi profiles.
Conceptually, Diamond Hard replication extends FAIR principles with computational verifiability: studies should not only share data and code but also furnish fixed-seed scripts, anchors, and machine-checkable tests that allow ongoing forensic audit of AI-assisted outputs. The approach draws on forensic audit practice and Gage repeatability and reproducibility (Gage R&R) in Six Sigma, recasting AI measurement as an instrument that must continuously prove its own reliability (MSI Certified, 2023). Beyond AMDG, the paper sketches how the same design—deterministic regeneration, anchors, multi-agent consensus, and continuous verification—can be applied to automated text coding, governance and ESG indices, behavioural experiments, and the computational components of health and drug-development workflows where trust and reproducibility are critical.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Workplace Safety: Compassionate AI as Harm Prevention
affiliations: Hong Kong Polytechnic University - School of Accounting and Finance, Georgia State University - J. Mack Robinson College of Business, Hong Kong Polytechnic University and University of California, San Diego

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence and Workplace Safety: Compassionate AI as Harm Prevention
detail.abstract: Investment in artificial intelligence (AI) is rising rapidly, yet little is known about how AI adoption affects a fundamental dimension of employee well-being: workplace safety. Conceptualizing compassion as care-oriented, harm-preventive action, we propose workforce-based AI adoption as a form of organizational compassionate AI-one that proactively protects workers from physical harm. Integrating the resource-based view and agency theory, we develop a framework linking workforcebased AI adoption to reductions in workplace safety violations through internal complementary resources and external accountability mechanisms. We operationalize workforce-based AI adoption using AI job posting intensity and the share of AI-skilled employees and test our hypotheses using a large archival dataset of 4,217 firms and 30,258 firm-year observations. Our findings show that greater workforce-based AI adoption is associated with fewer workplace safety violations, and that this relationship is significantly stronger in firms with greater internal complementary resources (e.g., safety training, dedicated safety teams, and formal safety policies) and stronger external monitoring (e.g., analyst coverage, ESG rating agency coverage, and media scrutiny). We further show that reductions in safety violations are associated with subsequent improvements in operational efficiency and ESG performance. Taken together, our findings suggest that, when embedded in appropriate organizational contexts, workforce-based AI can function as prevention-oriented compassionate AI that protects employees and their wellbeing while enhancing organizational performance and social responsibility.

title: Findings of Fact may be Stubborn things on Appeal, even if they are not Facts
affiliations: International Center for Law & Economics

detail.title: Findings of Fact may be Stubborn things on Appeal, even if they are not Facts

declarations.funderStatement: My funding is exclusively provided by my full-time salary, and was not specifically tied to this paper or project.

publicationDetails.detailsText: Concurrences, N° 1-2025 I On-Topic I The Google Search Decision: The Merits, Fate, and Potential Impact of the U.S. Court's Decision on Liability (Jan. 1, 2025)

detail.abstract: The U.S. government’s case in the Google Search matter raised complex questions of law and fact. The former are more likely issues for appeal, due in no small part to the trial court’s traditional function as finder of fact. The findings are interesting all the same—difficult, too, casual reactions to the decision notwithstanding. This paper critically reviews two types of evidence that were key to the government’s case. First is the evidence from behavioral economics on “search frictions” and the “stickiness” of default settings. Second are technical questions about scale advantages in the development or training of general search engines or related technology. I argue that the relevant evidence—especially that from behavioral economics—seemed more examples of scientism than science. That is not so much due to limitations in the underlying research on its own terms, as it is to the highly selective and radically overgeneralized presentation of that research.

title: Research on Multi-source Information Fusion and AI-Database Collaborative Tourism Attraction Recommendation Models
affiliations: Xinjiang Institute of Engineering, Xinjiang Institute of Engineering, Xinjiang Institute of Engineering, Xinjiang Institute of Engineering and Shandong Technology and Business University

detail.title: Research on Multi-source Information Fusion and AI-Database Collaborative Tourism Attraction Recommendation Models

keywords.keywords: travel recommendationsAI-Database collaborationMulti-source information fusiongraph neural networksattention mechanism

detail.abstract: The rapid development of smart tourism has led to challenges for online travel platforms, including information overload and difficulties in meeting personalized demands. Traditional recommendation methods suffer from poor accuracy due to data sparsity, cold-start problems, and insufficient integration of multi-source information. This paper proposes the Multi-source Information Fusion-Graph Neural Network-Attention Mechanism (MIF-GNN-ATT) model for tourist attraction recommendation. It integrates multi-source heterogeneous data, constructs deep relational representations via graph neural networks, performs feature fusion through attention mechanisms, and employs meta-learning strategies to address cold-start issues. Experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that compared to the optimal baseline model, the proposed model achieves Precision@10 and NDCG@10 improved by approximately 21.5% and 22.7%, respectively. The MySQL+Redis collaborative storage architecture enhances data utilization efficiency and system response performance, providing an effective solution for precise recommendations in smart tourism and offering insights for multi-source information fusion in recommendation systems.

title: AI Chatbots as Enablers of Effective Employee Onboarding
affiliations: Rashtrasant Tukdoji Maharaj Nagpur University

detail.title: AI Chatbots as Enablers of Effective Employee Onboarding
detail.abstract: Employee onboarding represents a critical juncture in the employment lifecycle, significantly influencing retention, productivity, and organizational culture integration. This research paper examines the transformative role of AI-powered chatbots in modernizing and enhancing the employee onboarding experience. Through analysis of recent implementations and scholarly discourse from 2024-2025, this study investigates how conversational AI technologies address traditional onboarding challenges, including information overload, scalability limitations, and inconsistent experiences. The findings reveal that AI chatbots facilitate personalized, accessible, and efficient onboarding processes while simultaneously reducing administrative burden on human resources teams. This paper explores the technological mechanisms underlying chatbot effectiveness, implementation strategies, measurable outcomes, and emerging challenges in this evolving domain. The research concludes that when strategically deployed, AI chatbots serve as powerful enablers of employee integration, though they function most effectively as complements to, rather than replacements for, human-centered onboarding practices.

title: Digital Financial Inclusion or Digital Financial Control? Power, Risk, and Governance in FinTech Expansion across the Global South
affiliations: University of Johanneburg

detail.title: Digital Financial Inclusion or Digital Financial Control? Power, Risk, and Governance in FinTech Expansion across the Global South
detail.abstract: FinTech has emerged as a central pillar of financial inclusion strategies across the Global South, promising expanded access to payments, credit, and financial services for previously excluded populations. While digital finance has delivered measurable gains in access and efficiency, growing evidence suggests that these benefits coexist with new forms of risk and inequality. This paper critically examines whether FinTech promotes genuine financial inclusion or instead generates new mechanisms of financial control and exclusion. Moving beyond access-based definitions, the analysis conceptualises inclusion in terms of agency, dignity, and protection. It identifies three key risks associated with FinTech expansion: data-driven surveillance, algorithmic bias and automated exclusion, and conditional access through digital identification systems. Drawing on a political economy perspective, the paper introduces the concept of digital financial colonialism to explain how value extraction, externalised risk, and asymmetric power relations shape outcomes in the Global South. The paper concludes that governance, rather than technology alone, determines whether FinTech advances inclusive and equitable development.

title: Human-Ai Symbiosis Dynamic Capabilities: A Proof-Of-Concept Case Study During Management Decision-Making Process In Dynamically Changing Environment
affiliations: Wrocław University of Science and Technology, Wrocław University of Science and Technology, Independent and

detail.title: Human-Ai Symbiosis Dynamic Capabilities: A Proof-Of-Concept Case Study During Management Decision-Making Process In Dynamically Changing Environment
detail.abstract: This article introduces Human-AI Symbiosis Dynamic Capabilities (HASDC) as a new construct in management sciences explaining how human-AI symbiosis systems adapt and create value under ambiguity. Extending dynamic capabilities theory and prior work on employee dynamic capabilities and AI capability as an organizational resource, it is argued that dominant perspectives still treat AI mainly as a tool and therefore not consider new class of AI systems: human-AI symbiosis, designed to sustain unresolved cognitive states, preserve ambiguity, and co-evolve with human sensemaking. The framework distinguishes human-AI symbiosis dynamic capabilities (meaning creation, decision grounding, bidirectional self-evolving adjustment), including AI-level dynamic capabilities (collective dreaming, truth gating, dynamic adjustment). The construct is a basis for a proof-of-concept case study in a small AI R&D company, where a CEO's year-long use of a human-AI symbiosis system as a cognitive partner enabled reframing an MVP strategy from architecture-first to demo-first. The case shows how weak signals were retained without premature closure, stabilized through epistemic governance, and translated into actionable readiness, supporting an anticipatory pivot later validated by collaboration opportunities. The study positions human-AI symbiosis as a distinct locus of dynamic capability formation and sets a basis for future operationalization and longitudinal validation.

title: Stirring Ripples Across the Lake: The Impact of AI Social Member's Comments on the Opinion Diversity
affiliations: Fudan University, Fudan University, University of Georgia - Department of Management Information Systems and School of Management, Fudan University

detail.title: Stirring Ripples Across the Lake: The Impact of AI Social Member's Comments on the Opinion Diversity
detail.abstract: Current studies on social bots have primarily focused on their functional advantages (such as moderation and information retrieval) or human-AI dyadic interactions and underexplored their more extensive social functions. We fill this gap by examining a new situation in which bots act like regular members in social groups, termed AI-bots as Social Members (ASMs), within online communities. Using data from a leading Asian social platform, we demonstrate that ASM participation significantly increases subsequent opinion diversity among human members. The characteristics of ASM-generated comments and ASMs' social identity jointly shape this effect. Specifically, subsequent human opinions diverge more when ASM's comments are emotionally neutral and consistent with prior human opinion. In contrast, human-generated comments with similar neutrality and consistency reduce opinion diversity, highlighting a fundamentally distinct social influence of ASM relative to human contributors. We also find that this effect is stronger when ASM participates autonomously and occupies a higher rank within the community. Additionally, ASM-induced opinion divergence is more pronounced in discussions centered on subjective topics and in communities characterized by higher modularity. We also step further to consider the consequences of ASM-induced opinion diversity. We find that while such opinion diversity fosters higher-quality content and innovation, it also increases offensive language. This research advances the understanding of human-AI interaction within social contexts and how bots can influence the dynamics of opinion formation.

title:
Intrinsic Value as Entropy-Bound Information 
A Quantum-Cryptographic Framework for Value Generation, Exchange, and Universal Commerce
affiliations: Independent

detail.title:
Intrinsic Value as Entropy-Bound Information 
A Quantum-Cryptographic Framework for Value Generation, Exchange, and Universal Commerce
detail.abstract: Modern economic systems lack a physically grounded definition of intrinsic value. Fiat currencies, subjective valuation models, and digitally scarce assets rely on belief, trust, or narrative coordination rather than enforceable physical constraints. This paper proposes a new framework in which intrinsic value is defined as entropy-bound information: information whose generation and persistence require irreversible physical processes. We formalize intrinsic value as information irreversibly instantiated and cryptographically bound to a verifiable state, independent of observers, institutions, or pricing mechanisms. We introduce the conceptual architecture of a Quantum Entropy Engine (QEE) as a value-generation mechanism capable of producing non-simulable, non-duplicable entropy through quantum measurement processes, and we distinguish value generation from value exchange by positioning blockchain systems strictly as accounting and transport layers. This framework reframes value as a conserved, physically constrained quantity rather than a subjective signal or policy variable. We examine the implications for inflation resistance, trust minimization, resource allocation, and post-fiat economic coordination. Mathematical formalism is introduced at a foundational level, with detailed proofs and implementation-specific considerations deferred to companion work.

title: Governing Generative Music: Attribution Limits, Platform Incentives, and the Future of Creator Income

detail.title: Governing Generative Music: Attribution Limits, Platform Incentives, and the Future of Creator Income
detail.abstract: Your favourite song may have already trained the AI that will replace its creator. Generative AI transforms recordings into training data, producing new tracks at near-zero marginal cost-while the artists who made those recordings receive nothing. How can creators be fairly compensated when their work trains systems that may eventually replace them? The problem is not primarily technical-watermarks fail, style cannot be copyrighted, and post-hoc detection faces fundamental limits (the "Oracle Problem"). Instead, the challenge is institutional: markets require signals of quality and provenance that current infrastructure cannot provide. Our central contribution is a two-friction taxonomy distinguishing administrative tasks (licensing, royalty tracking) that AI agents should automate from discovery processes (taste formation, identity expression) where human agency creates value. We propose attribution infrastructure not as perfect tracking but as a costly signal-verified human provenance becomes a market differentiator when AI-generated content floods the market. We outline a tiered framework (A0-A3) mapping attribution claims to existing identifiers, analyse how AI agents may paradoxically increase platform power without interoperability requirements, and offer concrete policy recommendations. The goal is governance that functions despite imperfect attribution: contractible provenance, competitive licensing rails, and clear property rights enabling creators and platforms to bargain efficiently.

title: Aid, Interrupted: Conflict Dynamics Following the USAID Suspension in Africa
affiliations: Reserve Bank of Australia, The University of Sydney and The University of Sydney

detail.title: Aid, Interrupted: Conflict Dynamics Following the USAID Suspension in Africa

declarations.funderStatement: Australian Research Council (DP240101563)

detail.abstract: Foreign aid withdrawal may put the stability of aid-dependent states at risk. Yet short-term conflict responses to donor-side aid disruptions remain poorly understood. We exploit the abrupt and unanticipated suspension of United States Agency for International Development (USAID) funding in January 2025 as an exogenous shock to examine its effects on conflict dynamics in Africa. Using monthly conflict data for 44 Sub-Saharan African countries, we apply event-study and difference-in-differences designs to trace conflict responses in highly aid-dependent countries relative to less aid-dependent countries following the suspension. We find a general elevation in conflict, with a statistically significant 15 percent increase in armed conflict between organized groups and up to a 10 percent increase in militia-perpetrated violence against civilians during the first six months following the USAID suspension. These effects vary systematically across institutional environments, suggesting that pre-existing state capacity shapes vulnerability to sudden aid disruptions.

title: The Critical Minerals Value Addition Myth: Why Mineral-Rich Countries may Struggle to Realize added Value
affiliations: ,  and University of Cambridge - Department of Engineering

detail.title: The Critical Minerals Value Addition Myth: Why Mineral-Rich Countries may Struggle to Realize added Value

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This material has been produced under the Climate Compatible Growth (CCG) programme, which is funded by UK aid from the UK government. However, the views expressed herein do not necessarily reflect the UK government's official policies.

detail.abstract: Critical minerals (CMs) are among the most important global value chains (GVCs) of the energy transition. Beyond their crucial role in reducing fossil fuel dependence, governments across the world and international organisations see them as an opportunity for mineral-rich countries to develop and join downstream sectors of the mineral GVC. While natural resources, under certain conditions, may drive value chain upgrading, turning the rising global demand for CMs into sustainable economic development is more complex than portrayed in the policy discourse. Incorporating the concepts of "conditions of production" and "conditions of exchange" from the Marxian political economy, with the Global Value Chains (GVC) framework from development economics, we examine the viability of value chain upgrading for countries with reserves of Nickel and Copper. Using Hausmann et al. 's (2023) Product Complexity Index (PCI), we have attempted to quantify the "conditions of production" needed to enter each stage of the mineral's GVC, as well as the current capacity of countries with significant mineral reserves. Secondly, using ownership data, we have quantified the "conditions of circulation" that determine trade relations and value distribution across the ten countries with the largest global reserves of copper and nickel. The findings suggest that many low-and middle-income countries with mineral resources have insufficient conditions of circulation and production to succeed in value-upgrading efforts within the energy transition timeline. While some countries with higher complexity may be able to join the GVC, "value capture" remains marginal under current GVC governance rules.

title: Beyond Pull-to-Center: How System Neglect Shapes Ordering Decisions Under Shifting Demand
affiliations: , Nova School of Business and Economics, Georgetown University - McDonough School of Business and IE Business School - IE University

detail.title: Beyond Pull-to-Center: How System Neglect Shapes Ordering Decisions Under Shifting Demand

declarations.funderStatement: This work was funded by Fundaçao para a Ciência e a Tecnologia (UIDB/00124/2020, UIDP/00124/2020 and Social Sciences DataLab - PINFRA/22209/2016), POR Lisboa and POR Norte (Social Sciences DataLab, PINFRA/22209/2016). The study was supported by the Ministerio de Ciencia e Innovación España [10.13039/501100011033, Grants HACOM - PID2022-138667OB-I00 and HDL-HS-280218].

detail.abstract: We examine how decision makers adjust newsvendor ordering decisions in response to demand signals that are indicative of a demand shift. Demand shifts driven by market changes, seasonality, or external shocks create uncertainty that decision makers frequently encounter in practice. By integrating models that explain the well-known pull-to-center (PTC) effect in static newsvendor environments with models of system neglect that explain how probability judgments react to signals indicative of a demand shift, we predict when PTC and system neglect mitigate versus amplify one another. Specifically, for high-margin products in stable environments with noisy signals and low-margin products in unstable environments with precise signals, system neglect and PTC effect tend to counteract each other, resulting in ordering decisions closer to optimal levels. In the remaining profit margin and demand environments, system neglect amplifies the underordering and overordering behavior resulting from the PTC effect. We test these predictions in experimental settings with uncensored and censored demand signals and find support for our model predictions. We explore the effectiveness of decision support systems and discuss implications for providing managerial interventions in environments with salient demand shifts.

title: Measurement Aware Predictive Maintenance Using Deep Learning: Modeling, Imbalance Handling, and Interpretability
affiliations: Helwan University, Helwan University, Students, Helwan University, Helwan University, Students and Helwan University, Helwan University, Students

detail.title: Measurement Aware Predictive Maintenance Using Deep Learning: Modeling, Imbalance Handling, and Interpretability
detail.abstract: Predictive maintenance has become a key enabler of intelligent industrial systems; however, its effectiveness strongly depends on the reliability and interpretation of measurement data. Many existing deep learning–based approaches assume ideal sensor availability and often overlook the impact of measurement uncertainty and class imbalance on maintenance decision-making. This paper proposes a measurement-aware deep learning framework for predictive maintenance that remains effective even in the absence of raw sensor signal measurements. Using the AI4I 2020 Predictive Maintenance Dataset, operational and condition-related variables are modeled as virtual measurement proxies, enabling systematic sensitivity and reliability analysis within a data-driven framework. To address the inherent rarity of failure events, a hybrid imbalance handling strategy combining SMOTE and cost-sensitive learning is employed. In addition, explainable artificial intelligence techniques are integrated to quantify the contribution of individual measurement proxies to failure prediction and maintenance decisions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves robust failure detection performance while maintaining stability under simulated measurement noise conditions. The findings emphasize the importance of measurement-driven modeling for developing reliable and interpretable predictive maintenance solutions in real industrial environments.

title: Dynamic Credit Risk Assessment under Carbon Transition Pressures: Evidence from Chinese Firms
affiliations: China Jiliang University, Monash University - Department of Econometrics & Business Statistics, Monash University - Department of Econometrics & Business Statistics and China Jiliang University

detail.title: Dynamic Credit Risk Assessment under Carbon Transition Pressures: Evidence from Chinese Firms
detail.abstract: The rapid transition to a low-carbon economy challenges traditional credit-risk assessment, especially in carbon-intensive industries. In this paper, we develop a dynamic framework that embeds carbon-transition exposure into corporate risk assessment. Sector-specific data envelopment analysis treats total greenhouse gas emission intensity as a negative (undesirable) input, producing interpretable carbon cost signals. We separate historical from expected performance using maximum-entropy time weights and peer-incentive adjustments, then classify firms with a topology-aware self-organizing map followed by K-means clustering. For 1,222 Chinese listed firms across 11 sectors during 2016-2021, we find that: (i) carbon intensity is the second-most important driver of efficiency after leverage, with substantial cross-sector heterogeneity; (ii) forward-looking scoring materially reorders mid-tier firms while the top and bottom deciles remain stable across reasonable settings of the time-preference parameter; and (iii) industries group into three patterns-history-expectation synchronization, expectation-dominant, and history-oriented.

title: Effectiveness of State Aid on Firm Performance: Evidence from the EU
affiliations: , European Union - European Investment Bank, European Union - European Investment Bank and European Union - European Investment Bank

detail.title: Effectiveness of State Aid on Firm Performance: Evidence from the EU
detail.abstract: Despite renewed interest in industrial policy, empirical evidence on state aid effectiveness remains limited. We examine the short-run effects of large state aid awards across 22 EU Member States, linking firm-level data from Orbis with publicly disclosed awards granted in 2017-2018. Using a generalized difference-indifferences design, we estimate effects on investment, employment, and productivity. State aid significantly increases capital investment, particularly among SMEs and firms receiving regional development aid, which are groups more likely to face financial constraints. Effects are strongest in Central and Eastern Europe. However, we find no corresponding improvements in productivity or employment within two years. These findings suggest that while state aid effectively stimulates investment in the short run, productivity gains may take longer to materialize, and efficiency gains could be obtained from better targeting and EU-wide coordination.

title: Annapolis and the Abbas-Olmert Direct Negotiations: A Critical Analysis
affiliations: Hebrew University of Jerusalem - Hebrew University

detail.title: Annapolis and the Abbas-Olmert Direct Negotiations: A Critical Analysis
detail.abstract: This article explains the events that brought about the meaningful negotiations between President Abbas and Prime Minister Olmert. Despite Olmert's good intentions and clear willingness to make peace by agreeing to unprecedented concessions, Olmert failed to convince Abbas to sign an agreement. The article opens by explaining the research methodology and the theoretical framework. It then explains the Annapolis conference and process including the three tiers of negotiations installed by Israel and the Palestinian Authority. While Olmert presented the best peace offer to date that any Israeli prime minister was willing to sign, it remained short of the Palestinian demands. A host of reasons led to yet another failure to resolve the Israeli-Palestinian conflict are analysed: the negotiations' structure, internal rivalries in Israel and the Palestinians, the continuation of the settlement project, Olmert's decision to embark on two wars, Olmert's illegitimate leadership due to his implication in corruption affairs, and Palestinian lack of trust in the Israeli government to deliver a long-lasting peace. The article concludes with a detailed assessment of the negotiation dynamics, aiming to distill key lessons that may inform future efforts should Israeli and Palestinian leaders re-enter serious peace talks.

title: Getting the Bad End of a Bilateral Bargain: The Administrative State Ignores Trump's Executive Order Prohibiting "Jawboning" of Private Speech
affiliations: Phoenix Center for Advanced Legal & Economic Public Policy Studies

detail.title: Getting the Bad End of a Bilateral Bargain: The Administrative State Ignores Trump's Executive Order Prohibiting "Jawboning" of Private Speech
detail.abstract: The Biden Administration had a well-documented reputation for using the “vast powers” of the administrative state to coerce private speech. Immediately upon taking office, President Trump sent a clear message that a new sheriff was in town by issuing an Executive Order expressly directing that “no Federal Government officer, employee, or agent engages in or facilitates any conduct that would unconstitutionally abridge the free speech of any American citizen” and that no taxpayer resources can be “used to engage in or facilitate any conduct that would  unconstitutionally abridge the free speech of any American citizen.” Unfortunately, the administrative state has yet to comply. This article presents several case studies demonstrating how private firms agreed to “voluntary” merger conditions curtailing their speech as a necessary prerequisite for getting their transactions approved by the government. This article concludes that while Americans voted for change in 2024, having the Trump administration’s antitrust and regulatory agencies emulate the jawboning behavior of the previous administration is no change at all.

title: The Association between Employee's Subjective Well-being and Psychosocial Working Environment

detail.title: The Association between Employee's Subjective Well-being and Psychosocial Working Environment

declarations.ethicsApproval: The research data was collected on a voluntary and anonymous basis. All respondents were informed about the purpose and description of the research and gave their informed consent to participate in it before starting to fill out the questionnaires on a specialized Internet platform (anketolog.ru). The collected data were processed and analyzed anonymously.
declarations.funderStatement: This article was prepared with the support of a grant from the Russian Science Foundation as part of project № 22-1800452-P “Psychological design of the workspace as a factor in the employee subjective well-being and the innovative potential of the organization”.

detail.abstract: The subjective well-being of employees is one of the key factors in the long-term sustainability and effectiveness of an organization. The purpose of this study is to identify a set of specific factors in the psychosocial environment of an organization that are interrelated with the subjective well-being of its employees. The study was conducted on a Main sample (N=325) and an independent Control sample (N=100) of adult respondents from the main regions and sectors of the Russian economy. The factors of the psychosocial working environment of the organization were measured using the DPQ questionnaire, the well-being of employees was measured using the PERMA+4 technic. The association was analyzed with linear and nonlinear modeling. The study showed that the employee's subjective well-being is associated with the following parameters of the psychosocial environment: "Organizational justice and leadership quality"; "Role clarity"; "Absence of unnecessary work tasks"; "Interaction, trust, and support from colleagues and managers"; and "Possibilities for development". The obtained results may be used to design a workspace that enhances employee well-being, as well as the long-term sustainability and effectiveness of the organization.

title: IntelliFi: Intelligent Execution of Monetary Theory
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: IntelliFi: Intelligent Execution of Monetary Theory
detail.abstract: Monetary theory has historically focused on the objectives of money—stability, coordination, and value preservation—while leaving the execution of monetary policy largely dependent on discretionary institutions or static rule-based systems. This paper argues that the absence of a formal execution layer constitutes a structural gap in modern monetary systems. We introduce IntelliFi (Intelligent Finance) as a general framework for the intelligent execution of monetary theory. IntelliFi treats money not as a static object or purely institutional construct, but as a closed-loop control system in which issuance, incentives, stabilization mechanisms, and policy enforcement are executed through adaptive, feedback-driven, constraint-bound, and verifiable processes. Unlike traditional fiat systems, which rely on human discretion, or algorithmic monetary systems, which rely on rigid pre-commitments, IntelliFi formalizes monetary execution as a bounded optimization problem governed by explicit constitutional constraints. Intelligence, in this context, is defined not as autonomy or artificial decision-making, but as systematic responsiveness to observable economic signals within non-negotiable limits. The paper presents a formal definition of IntelliFi, outlines its execution model, and identifies the necessary and sufficient conditions for a monetary system to qualify as IntelliFi-compliant. Existing monetary regimes—including commodity money, fiat systems, cryptocurrencies, decentralized finance protocols, and governance-based systems—are examined as partial or proto-executions of IntelliFi principles. By separating monetary theory from its execution and formalizing execution as a first-class economic problem, this work reframes how monetary systems can be designed, evaluated, and governed. IntelliFi is presented not as a new currency or policy prescription, but as a general purpose framework for implementing monetary theory in adaptive, transparent, and resilient ways.

title: Nature and Importance of Job Satisfaction
affiliations: University of Tetovo

detail.title: Nature and Importance of Job Satisfaction
detail.abstract: Recently there has been a resurgence of interest in the analysis of job satisfaction variables. Job satisfaction is correlated with labor market behavior such as productivity, quits and absenteeism. In this paper a general measure of job satisfaction is analysed in raltion to several personal and job characteristics. The data used are from a survey conducted with 40 employees from different types of companies from the Pollog region in the Republic of North Macedonia. The connection between age, experience, gender and education with job satisfaction are considered as partof the paper. Keywords: age, gender, sex, job satisfaction.

title: Online Linear Programming with Replenishment
affiliations: , Tsinghua University - Yau Mathematical Sciences Center, Bytedance Inc., Tsinghua University, Students, Bytedance Inc. and Bytedance Inc.

detail.title: Online Linear Programming with Replenishment
detail.abstract:
We study an online linear programming (OLP) model in which inventory is not provided upfront but instead arrives gradually through an exogenous stochastic replenishment process. This replenishment-based formulation captures operational settings, such as e-commerce fulfillment, perishable supply chains, and renewable-powered systems, where resources are accumulated gradually and initial inventories are small or zero. The introduction of dispersed, uncertain replenishment fundamentally alters the structure of classical OLPs, creating persistent stockout risk and eliminating advance knowledge of the total budget. 
    We develop new algorithms and regret analyses for three major distributional regimes studied in the OLP literature: bounded distributions, finite-support distributions, and continuous-support distributions with a non-degeneracy condition. For bounded distributions, we design an algorithm that achieves $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrt{T})$ regret. For finite-support distributions with a non-degenerate induced LP, we obtain $\mathcal{O}(\log T)$ regret, and we establish an $\Omega(\sqrt{T})$ lower bound for degenerate instances, demonstrating a sharp separation from the classical setting where $\mathcal{O}(1)$ regret is achievable. For continuous-support, non-degenerate distributions, we develop a two-stage accumulate-then-convert algorithm that achieves $\mathcal{O}(\log^2 T)$ regret, comparable to the $\mathcal{O}(\log T)$ regret in classical OLPs. Together, these results provide a near-complete characterization of the optimal regret achievable in OLP with replenishment. Finally, we empirically evaluate our algorithms and demonstrate their advantages over natural adaptations of classical OLP methods in the replenishment setting.

title: Technology Acceptance of Advanced Materials and Nanomaterials in Public Organizations in Old Industrial Regions: A Conceptual Framework Authors
affiliations: , University of Ostrava, University of Ostrava, University of Ostrava, University of Ostrava and University of Ostrava

detail.title: Technology Acceptance of Advanced Materials and Nanomaterials in Public Organizations in Old Industrial Regions: A Conceptual Framework Authors

declarations.funderStatement: This publication is supported by the ESF in the „Advanced Materials for Energy and Environmental Technologies“ project, reg. nr. CZ.02.01.01/00/23_021/0008592 within the Programme Johannes Amos Comenius.“

detail.abstract: Public organizations operating in old industrial regions often face persistent institutional constraints that complicate the adoption of advanced materials and nanomaterials. This paper develops a conceptual framework for analyzing technological acceptance in such regions. Building on the Technology-Organization-Environment perspective, the framework integrates organizational conditions with individual-level cognitive and sociocultural factors to capture the multi-level nature of adoption processes in public-sector settings. The paper argues that technology acceptance in public organizations cannot be adequately explained as a linear managerial decision but rather emerges from interactions between historically embedded institutional structures and heterogeneous individual interpretations of technological change. By emphasizing contextualized institutional agency, the framework contributes to a more nuanced understanding of technology acceptance in lagging regions. The study further discusses implications for innovation policy, public procurement, and regional development strategies. The analytical model presented here serves as a foundation for subsequent empirical investigation and is intended as a basis for further theoretical and applied research.

title: Optimal Liability Design for Medical AI
affiliations: Nanjing University - School of Management and Engineering, University of Tennessee, Knoxville - Haslam College of Business and Nanjing University - School of Management and Engineering

detail.title: Optimal Liability Design for Medical AI
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into medical decision-making, yet its liability implications remain complex, particularly when physicians differ in diagnostic skills and their quality is unobservable. This paper develops a principal-agent model in which a social planner designs medical liability to regulate a physician with private quality information who chooses between a standard treatment, a personalized judgment-based treatment, or following an imperfect AI recommendation. Our analysis yields several novel insights. First, we show that the optimal mechanism under asymmetric information is surprisingly simple: a uniform, one-size-fits-all liability level for all physician types who deviate from the standard of care. Despite physician heterogeneity, this simple policy often achieves the full-information first-best outcome, particularly when standard care is reliable or AI is highly accurate. Second, the relationship between AI accuracy and optimal liability is non-monotonic. Contrary to common intuition, better AI does not always imply more relaxed liability. As AI accuracy increases, the optimal liability either decreases monotonically or follows an inverted-U pattern, depending on the uncertainty of the standard treatment. Third, asymmetric information does not universally reduce social welfare. Welfare loss arises only when standard care is unreliable and AI accuracy is too low; even then, its magnitude follows an inverted U-shape, initially increasing as AI complicates the regulatory problem, but declining as more accurate AI helps mitigate it. Finally, we find that information asymmetry is a double-edged sword in the presence of AI, and greater transparency does not benefit all stakeholders equally.

title: PI – Management System: PDCA and Artificial Intelligence
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: PI – Management System: PDCA and Artificial Intelligence

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no personal, financial, or institutional conflicts of interest related to this work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human participants, patients, personal data, or experimental interventions and therefore did not require ethics committee approval.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
Institutions increasingly operate in environments marked by growing complexity, regulatory density, and accelerated decision-making cycles. While data volumes, formal norms, and reporting requirements continue to expand, many organizational decisions remain fragmented, weakly traceable, and highly dependent on individual interpretation. At the same time, Artificial Intelligence has been informally adopted by individuals and departments, often without institutional governance, accountability, or integration into management systems.

This paper proposes the PI – Management System, a conceptual framework designed to integrate Artificial Intelligence into institutional management in a structured, responsible, and human-centered manner. Rather than treating AI as an isolated tool or automation mechanism, the PI positions it as a transversal cognitive mediator embedded within the PDCA (Plan–Do–Check–Act) cycle, supporting analysis, coherence, and continuous improvement.

A central element of the model is the Principle of Final Human Ratification, which establishes that no relevant decision mediated by Artificial Intelligence may be executed without explicit human validation and responsibility. The PI is presented as an evolution of traditional management systems for complex and regulated environments, enhancing decision quality while preserving institutional accountability and legitimacy.

title: Mitigating Agency Problems or Restricting Managerial Flexibility: The Effects of Bond Covenants on Operational Efficiency
affiliations: College of Business, Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST),  and College of Business, Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST)

detail.title: Mitigating Agency Problems or Restricting Managerial Flexibility: The Effects of Bond Covenants on Operational Efficiency
detail.abstract: As the bond market has grown, bond covenants have become more prevalent. These covenants mitigate agency problems between shareholders and creditors by limiting managers' risky behavior. However, such restrictions may also limit managerial flexibility, potentially impeding the firm's capacity to execute effective business policies and operations. This study empirically investigates the impact of bond covenants on firms' operational efficiency. Using a comprehensive dataset of U.S. public bonds issued between 1998 and 2019, our findings suggest that financing restrictions included in covenants enhance operational efficiency, whereas investment restrictions negatively affect operational efficiency. Further analysis reveals that the positive impact of financing restrictions is primarily evident in firms with limited growth opportunities, whereas the negative impact of investment restrictions is pronounced in firms with high growth potential. By revealing how bond contracts shape firms' operational performance, we extend the understanding of how restrictions on financing and investment activities affect operational outcomes.

title: Geography of Social Enterprises in Cultural and Creative Industries in Italy
affiliations: and

detail.title: Geography of Social Enterprises in Cultural and Creative Industries in Italy

publicationDetails.journalName: Euricse Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: This research explores the spatial distribution of cultural and creative social enterprises (CCSE) in Italy. Specifically, the aim is to answer the following research questions: (1) How are social enterprises in the cultural and creative industries distributed across Italy? (2) What factors influence this distribution? The study draws on the literature on creative economy and social enterprises to explore these issues. Firm-level data from the Aida-Bureau van Dijk database and the Third Sector Single National Register (RUNTS) are used. The analysis employs aggregated data at the provincial level (NUTS-3). Geographical patterns are analysed through location quotients and Moran's I test, while ordinary least squares regression is used to identify possible socioeconomic determinants. The findings reveal the absence of the typical North-South divide in the distribution of CCSE clusters across Italian provinces and point out a complex interplay between demand and supply factors behind it.

title: Why Pedagogy Is Not Enough: Institutional Homeostasis and Circulation in Education

detail.title: Why Pedagogy Is Not Enough: Institutional Homeostasis and Circulation in Education
detail.abstract:
Debates on educational reform are commonly framed through the contrast between Rational Systems (RS) and Natural Systems (NS): structure versus culture, metrics versus relationships. In practice, this distinction is often reduced to a moralized taxonomy rather than an operational account. RS becomes shorthand for bureaucracy, control, and incentives; NS for care and community. What disappears is an explanation of why reform so often disappoints—why pedagogical transformation coexists with stable institutional outcomes. 

This paper argues that the RS/NS frame is incomplete because it omits the institution’s operating layer. Educational systems persist not only through rules or culture, but through circulation and homeostasis: fiscal pathways that determine capacity, and informational pathways that determine what becomes legible, actionable, and accountable. When reform alters surface grammar—classroom language, pedagogical style, professional discourse—without rewiring these circulatory systems, the institution returns to equilibrium. To render this operating layer analytically visible, the paper introduces two complementary lenses. Fiscal Epistemology (FE) explains why institutions act only on admissible, decision-grade information rather than on intentions or values. Fiscal Geometry (FG) describes education as a routing system and reform as path reconfiguration, allowing failure to be understood as tension-driven reversion under unchanged circulation. The core claim is concrete: reform fails less because people do not believe, and more because circulation remains unchanged. In AI-mediated institutions, this gap becomes decisive: reforms that do not alter circulation become computationally invisible.

title: The Epistemology of Fear: Understanding Its Role in Shaping Choices and Control in Outsourcing
affiliations: Independent Scholar

detail.title: The Epistemology of Fear: Understanding Its Role in Shaping Choices and Control in Outsourcing

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA
declarations.ethicsApproval: NA
declarations.funderStatement: NA

detail.abstract: Fear is commonly understood as an emotional reaction to perceived threat, yet its epistemological significance remains underexplored. This article develops an epistemology of fear to examine how fear shapes knowledge, judgment, and decision-making in outsourcing contexts. Drawing on neuroscience, philosophy of emotion, social theory, and organizational analysis, it argues that fear functions as an epistemic force that structures attention, narrows interpretative horizons, and stabilizes power relations under conditions of uncertainty and knowledge asymmetry. In outsourcing environments, fear emerges not merely as an individual response but as a structural and socially mediated phenomenon reinforced through governance mechanisms, performance metrics, and narratives of inevitability. By distinguishing between experiential and anticipatory fear and situating fear among other epistemic emotions, the article shows how fear constrains epistemic agency and facilitates conformity while appearing rational from within organizational frameworks. The paper concludes that addressing fear is not only a managerial or psychological task but an ethical responsibility grounded in epistemic autonomy. By reframing outsourcing as a knowledge practice shaped by emotional and epistemic conditions, this study contributes to broader debates on organizational decision-making, power, and responsibility in contexts of uncertainty.

title: Green or Red? Designing ESG Audit Information Disclosure for Investment Risk Sharing
affiliations: New Jersey Institute of Technology, University of California, San Diego (UCSD) - Rady School of Management and Tel-Aviv University

detail.title: Green or Red? Designing ESG Audit Information Disclosure for Investment Risk Sharing
detail.abstract:
Problem definition: Retailers increasingly face exposure to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) risks arising from upstream manufacturers' production practices. To mitigate these risks, large retailers often able to obtain rich, proprietary information about their manufacturers' ESG performance through repeated interaction and internal monitoring. Yet, in practice, they frequently rely on third-party ESG audits that provide only coarse and noisy labels. This paper studies why delegating ESG information disclosure to a less informative auditor can be optimal for the retailers. 

Methodology/results: We develop a supply-chain model in which a manufacturer's ESG performance is stochastic and depends on costly investment. A retailer can either audit the manufacturer directly and fully observe ESG outcomes, or delegate disclosure to an auditor who commits ex ante to a coarse labeling rule. The retailer contracts with the manufacturer based on ESG label reported by the auditor, and the manufacturer exerts effort based on the anticipation of relationship between effort and information disclosure. We show that the retailer direct audit, i.e., full disclosure, results in no trade following an unfavorable ESG realization, leading to underinvestment in ESG effort by the manufacturer. By contrast, auditor mediated disclosure can optimally involve partial or full pooling, expanding the set of realizations under which trade occurs and strengthening upstream investment incentives. As a result, coarse ESG labels can increase equilibrium effort and improve expected payoffs for both the retailer and the manufacturer relative to retailer direct audit. 

Managerial implications: We further characterize how optimal disclosure responds to product value, manufacturer financial incentives, and ESG penalty severity. Higher product value leads to less precise audit policy but higher induced effort, while stronger penalties increase disclosure precision but reduce ESG investment. These results highlight the trade-off between information precision and incentive provision, and provide a new rationale for the prevalence of coarse ESG audits in supply

title: Taming Tail Risk in Financial Markets: Conformal Risk Control for Nonstationary Portfolio VaR
affiliations: University of Oxford

detail.title: Taming Tail Risk in Financial Markets: Conformal Risk Control for Nonstationary Portfolio VaR
detail.abstract: Risk forecasts drive trading constraints and capital allocation, yet losses are nonstationary and regime-dependent. This paper studies sequential one-sided VaR control via conformal calibration. I propose regime-weighted conformal risk control (RWC), which calibrates a safety buffer from past forecast errors using exponential time decay and regime-similarity weights from regime features. RWC is model-agnostic and wraps any conditional quantile forecaster to target a desired exceedance rate. Finite-sample coverage is established under weighted exchangeability, and approximation bounds are derived under smoothly drifting regimes. On the CRSP U.S. equity portfolio, time-weighted conformal calibration is a strong default under drift, while regime weighting can improve regime-conditional stability in some settings with modest conservativeness changes.

title: Fifty Years of Knowledge Management Research: A System-Level Analysis of Intellectual, Conceptual and Social Structures
affiliations: Academia Forţelor Terestre „Nicolae Bălcescu”, Academia Forţelor Terestre „Nicolae Bălcescu”, Academia Forţelor Terestre „Nicolae Bălcescu”, Academia Forţelor Terestre „Nicolae Bălcescu” and Lucian Blaga University of Sibiu

detail.title: Fifty Years of Knowledge Management Research: A System-Level Analysis of Intellectual, Conceptual and Social Structures
detail.abstract: Knowledge Management (KM) has evolved over the last five decades as a complex sociotechnical system shaped by interactions between organizational processes, technologies and social actors. This study maps the systemic evolution of KM research between 1975 and 2025 by examining its intellectual, conceptual and social subsystems. Using a largescale bibliometric science-mapping approach that combines performance indicators and network-based techniques, we analyze 33,153 documents indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection. The results reveal a pronounced post-1995 expansion of the field, marked by a consolidated core of specialized journals and influential scholars, alongside an increasingly global research network. The analysis shows that KM research is structured around four interdependent dimensions: organizational processes, strategic orientations, technological infrastructures and socio-cultural factors. More recent developments indicate the emergence of new system trajectories associated with digital transformation, knowledge governance and sustainability. Viewed through a system-level lens, these findings position KM as an evolving research system characterized by adaptive and cross-domain dynamics.

title: Global Fractures: Economic Implications of the U.S.–China Trade War on Global Supply Chains and Domestic Economy.
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Global Fractures: Economic Implications of the U.S.–China Trade War on Global Supply Chains and Domestic Economy.
detail.abstract: The last decade marks one of the most transformative period in global trade history. Triggered by the U.S.–China trade war, and waves of tariff escalations and protectionist policies have led to the disruption established trade routes, reshaped production networks, and redefined the dynamics of globalization. This paper examines the multifaceted effects of trade wars on global supply chains through a data-driven analysis of trade flows, foreign direct investment (FDI), and global value chain (GVC) participation. By using secondary data from  verified websites such as OECD, UNCTAD, IMF, and WTO databases, this study visualizes key trends through comparative graphs and country-level assessments. These findings reveal significant trade diversion toward emerging economies such as Vietnam, India, and Mexico and shows a structural shift toward regionalized production models. This paper also explores how global crises like COVID-19 accelerated the move from efficiency-driven supply chains to resilience-based frameworks. The study concludes that while trade wars have fragmented globalization, they have also sparked adaptive realignments that may redefine global economic interdependence in the decade ahead.

title: A Game-Theoretic Analysis of the Minnesota Paradox: Equilibrium of Exclusion and Resistance Driven by Statistical Errors and Information Asymmetry
affiliations: Rodem Asset Co.,Ltd. CEO

detail.title: A Game-Theoretic Analysis of the Minnesota Paradox: Equilibrium of Exclusion and Resistance Driven by Statistical Errors and Information Asymmetry
detail.abstract: This paper analyzes the escalating immigration conflict in Minnesota, specifically focusing on the massive "Feeding Our Future" fraud scandal involving the Somali community. By employing statistical decision theory and game theory, this study elucidates the structural mechanism behind the conflict between the federal government's exclusionist policies and the local residents' resistance. We demonstrate that the conflict stems from a fundamental difference in risk tolerance regarding Type I and Type II errors and a breakdown in signaling mechanisms due to information asymmetry. Finally, we propose "Minnesota Model 2.0," a mechanism design based on a separating equilibrium, as a concrete solution to resolve the current deadlock.

title: On a Common Misconception about Count Data Models in Empirical OM Research: A Review and Practical Guide
affiliations: and Dongbei University of Finance and Economics

detail.title: On a Common Misconception about Count Data Models in Empirical OM Research: A Review and Practical Guide

declarations.funderStatement: 1. C. Fang’s work is funded by the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG, Ger- man Research Foundation) under Germany’s Excellence Strategy – EXC-2047/1 – 390685813. 2. J. Gao’s work is funded by National Natural Science Foundation of China – 72402030.

detail.abstract: Count data problems are prevalent in the empirical research of Operations Management (OM). Maximum Likelihood (ML) estimators of Poisson and Negative Binomial (NB) models are typically applied to approach count data problems. There is, however, a common misconception: NB models must be applied instead of Poisson models whenever a significant over-dispersion is detected in data. In fact, it has long been proven that Poisson ML estimators remain consistent under distributional misspecification, provided that the conditional mean is correctly specified. To avoid the potential invalid inference from misspecified conditional variance, researchers can simply compute robust standard errors, rendering the Quasi-Poisson ML estimators. In this paper, we clarify the harmful consequences of the misconception, especially non-convergence issue of NB estimators. However, we also underscore the limitations of the Quasi-Poisson ML estimators, such as failure to predict the exact probabilities for each count value. We thereby propose a practical guide on how to rigorously run count data models in R and Stata.

title: HIEU: Regime-aware Hypernetwork Experts for Explainable Multi-Asset Cryptocurrency Forecasting
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, , affiliation not provided to SSRN and Lecturer

detail.title: HIEU: Regime-aware Hypernetwork Experts for Explainable Multi-Asset Cryptocurrency Forecasting
detail.abstract:
Despite promising results from state-of-the-art general time-series predictive models, their direct applications in cryptofinance are undermined by the lack of domain-specific consideration of multi-asset interactions, cryptocurrency regimes, and model explainability for reliable decision-making. Therefore, we propose HIEU, a novel hypernetwork of experts that dynamically generates context-conditioned low-rank weight adaptations based on a rich multi-view context vector fusing regime, time-evolving cross-asset graph relationships, and multi-scale frequency patterns. Our approach enables sample-specific, regime-aware forecasting that captures temporal shifts while remaining parameter-efficient. Notably, HIEU offers intrinsic glass-box explainability through interpretable regime probabilities, graph heatmaps, frequency gating weights, and optional post-hoc analysis on the context vector, ultimately delivering probabilistic quantile predictions tailored for risk-sensitive multi-asset cryptocurrency trading. Having outperformed prominent time-series Transformers and deep learning variants in validation metrics alongside architectural design, HIEU advances the engineering of adaptive, explainable forecasting models for real-world financial trading platforms.Code for26
