title: Can the Federal Communications Commission Preempt State AI Laws? A Review of the Communications Act and Interpreting Caselaw
affiliations: Phoenix Center for Advanced Legal & Economic Public Policy Studies

detail.title: Can the Federal Communications Commission Preempt State AI Laws? A Review of the Communications Act and Interpreting Caselaw
detail.abstract:
Efforts to regulate Artificial Intelligence (“AI”) at the state level are
proliferating like mushrooms after it rains. Unfortunately, given the lack of a clear
statement by Congress that the federal government can preempt such state AI laws, current
legal options to stop the proliferation of state AI regulation are shaky at best. Grasping for
straws, the Trump AI Action Plan offers the following legal strategy to stop the legislative
proliferation: the Federal Communications Commission (“FCC”) should “evaluate
whether state AI regulations interfere with the agency’s ability to carry out its obligations
and authorities under the Communications Act of 1934.” As detailed below, given the plain
language of the Communications Act as well as the present state of the caselaw, it is highly
unlikely the FCC will succeed in these efforts. Thus, to prevent AI being subject to a
patchwork of state laws, Congress should move expeditiously to enact a cohesive federal
AI framework that can preempt such laws. This paper is organized as follows. First the
paper details the statutory language in the Communications Act highlighted by the Trump
AI Action plan. Next, the paper goes through efforts to use the FCC’s efforts to preempt
state laws governing municipal broadband. The next several sections proceed to go
through the FCC’s efforts of “preemption by nonregulation”—that is, rather than make
case-specific preemption decisions, the FCC attempted to deregulate whole swaths of the
industry by reclassifying those services as “information services” under Title I of the
Communications Act. These reclassification battles, in turn, led to the two-decade Net
Neutrality debate. Paradoxically, the FCC’s reclassification of broadband as Title I services
severely curtailed (if not outright eliminated) the FCC’s authority to preempt states’ efforts
to regulate the provision of broadband. The paper concludes by noting that because the
clock is ticking, trying to contort the Communications Act to preempt the growing
patchwork of disparate state AI laws is a Quixotic exercise in futility. Worse, as courts are
often a “black box” where outcomes can be unexpected, engaging in legal gymnastics with
the Communications Act could perversely lead to a vast expansion of the FCC’s authority
beyond its statutory constraints. The cleanest legal solution, therefore, is for Congress to
enact expeditiously some sort of preemption mechanism before the United States loses the
AI race due to an unnecessary “Death by Fifty State Cuts.”

title: Understanding Landowner Perceptions: Enhancing Conservation Easement Adoption in Missouri's Priority Landscapes
affiliations: University of Missouri at Columbia - University of Missouri School of Law, University of Missouri, University of Missouri, University of Missouri at Columbia, Independent and Independent

detail.title: Understanding Landowner Perceptions: Enhancing Conservation Easement Adoption in Missouri's Priority Landscapes

declarations.ethicsApproval: This manuscript presents human subjects research approved by the University of Missouri Institutional Review Board, Project #2025528.

detail.abstract: Conservation of private lands is essential for protecting open space, supporting ecosystems and species, preserving resources, and facilitating outdoor recreation. One tool for private land conservation is a conservation easement-a voluntary legal agreement where a landowner surrenders certain rights to use or develop their property. This study explores landowner perceptions of perpetual conservation easements in areas of high conservation value in Missouri, focusing on landowners without existing easements. Through interviews, four themes emerge containing both motivations and constraints: prior knowledge, land protection, regulations, and finance. Many landowners were unfamiliar with conservation easements or had misconceptions or misunderstandings. The results contribute to the limited body of qualitative research on conservation easements, while identifying broader themes relevant to other geographies. The results can inform policymakers, government agencies, land trusts, and private landowners. This study concludes that further public outreach and education would support conservation easement adoption.

title: The Attractiveness of Youth Groups that are Sympathetic or Unsympathetic to Struggles Relating to Social Media, Pornography, and Online Gaming
affiliations: Azusa Pacific University, Azusa Pacific University and Azusa Pacific University

detail.title: The Attractiveness of Youth Groups that are Sympathetic or Unsympathetic to Struggles Relating to Social Media, Pornography, and Online Gaming

declarations.ethicsApproval: This study was granted Exempt Status by the Institutional Review Board of Azusa Pacific University (IRB ID # 25-113).

detail.abstract: Each generation faces its own set of challenges. Generation Z faces unprecedented challenges with social media, pornography, and online gaming. These struggles may be contributing factors to the difficulty that churches have in retaining youth. This paper examines the attractiveness of church youth groups, comparing those that are sympathetic to the struggles of Generation Z to those that are unsympathetic. An online survey of both Christian and non-Christian adults (N = 165) indicated that sympathetic youth groups were more attractive than unsympathetic ones. When looking at the data from just non-Christians, this preference remained the same. The unattractiveness of unsympathetic youth groups was especially strong for younger participants. This implies that youth groups that can be sympathetic to the struggles of Generation Z without compromising the gospel are likely to grow more rapidly than those that are unsympathetic.

title: Heaven or Earth? The Evolving Role of Global Shocks for Domestic Monetary Policy
affiliations: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - Sloan School of Management, World Bank and World Bank

detail.title: Heaven or Earth? The Evolving Role of Global Shocks for Domestic Monetary Policy

publicationDetails.journalName: MIT Sloan School of Management Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: Business cycles are increasingly driven by global shocks, rather than the domestic demand shocks prominent in earlier decades, posing challenges for central banks seeking to meet domestic mandates and communicate their policy decisions. This paper analyzes the evolving influence and characteristics of global and domestic shocks in advanced economies from 1970-2024 using a new FAVAR model that decomposes movements in interest rates, inflation, and output growth into four global shocks (demand, supply, oil, and monetary policy) and three domestic shocks (demand, supply, and monetary policy). We find that the role of global shocks has increased sharply over time and that their characteristics differ from those of domestic shocks across multiple dimensions. Compared to domestic shocks, global shocks have a larger supply component, higher variance, more persistent effects on inflation, and are more asymmetric (contributing more to tightening than to easing phases of monetary policy). As global supply shocks have become more prominent, central banks have also been less willing to "look through" their effects on inflation than for comparable domestic shocks. The distinct characteristics and rising influence of global shocks-particularly global supply shocks-have significant implications for modeling monetary policy and designing central bank frameworks.

title: Fortifying Servant Leadership’s Foundations: Five Core Questions to Guide Future Research
affiliations: University at Buffalo, Monash University, Central Michigan University, Georgia State University and University of Mississippi

detail.title: Fortifying Servant Leadership’s Foundations: Five Core Questions to Guide Future Research

declarations.ethicsApproval: Consent
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: Servant leadership research is rapidly accumulating, but the degree to which it advances the broader leadership literature with novel insights remains a contentious point of debate. Skeptics argue that the validity of servant leadership’s theoretical foundation and its empirical measures are questionable. Supporters, however, point to servant leadership’s unique focus on service to multiple stakeholders as well as meta-analyses supporting its incremental predictive validity relative to other moral and inspirational leadership approaches as evidence of its novelty in the leadership domain. These two camps seldom engage in constructive dialogue to advance the field in a purposeful, productive, and practical way. The purpose of this editorial is a twofold approach to bridge this gap. First, we introduce a servant leadership special issue in Group and Organization Management (GOM) that brings together emerging and established scholars, as well as a seasoned practitioner, to address shortcomings in extant servant leadership scholarship and articulate new ideas that promise to usher the literature into a new era of insights. Second, we discuss five core questions to fortify the foundations of servant leadership research. These questions pertain to servant leadership’s nomological network, empirical and theoretical overlap with other leadership constructs, theoretical boundaries, dimensionality, and empirical validity.We hope this GOM special issue and editorial paint a constructive and promising path forward for the next era of servant leadership research and practice.

title: The Complete Mathematics of Transformers and In-Context Learning: A Unified Rigorous Treatment with Full Derivations and Proofs
affiliations: Artificial Intelligence in Finance Institute

detail.title: The Complete Mathematics of Transformers and In-Context Learning: A Unified Rigorous Treatment with Full Derivations and Proofs
detail.abstract: We provide a unified rigorous mathematical treatment of transformer architectures and in-context learning (ICL) with complete proofs for all results. This document synthesizes transformer architecture theory with ICL foundations, establishing: (i) a group-theoretic characterization of permutation-equivariant maps with explicit dimension counting; (ii) sub-exponential concentration of dot products and the resulting 1/ √ d k scaling; (iii) global Lipschitz bounds for softmax via its Fisher-metric Jacobian; (iv) spectral theory of doubly stochastic operators for manifold-constrained hyper-connections; (v) self-attention as gradient flow on the sphere with rigorous Lyapunov analysis; (vi) constructive proofs that linear attention implements gradient descent; (vii) the precise correspondence between softmax attention and Nadaraya-Watson kernel regression; (viii) information-theoretic bounds on learnability from context; and (ix) universal approximation with explicit depth/width rates. The central thesis is that transformers implement flows on manifolds (attention as gradient flow on S d-1), stabilized by isometries (RoPE rotations, doubly stochastic mixing, variance-preserving scaling), performing metaoptimization via kernel methods (ICL as non-parametric regression).

title: Whispers of the Divine: The Most Provocative Verses of the Hebrew Bible
affiliations: City University of New York (CUNY) - Koppelman School of Business and City University of New York (CUNY) - Paul H. Chook Department of Information Systems & Statistics

detail.title: Whispers of the Divine: The Most Provocative Verses of the Hebrew Bible
detail.abstract: This paper examines profound passages from the Hebrew Bible that convey enduring spiritual, ethical, and leadership wisdom through remarkably economical language. By analyzing texts from Genesis to Esther, we explore how fundamental human values are distilled into brief declarations that continue to resonate today. These verses address timeless themes such as human dignity, justice, and compassion for the vulnerable. We demonstrate how these ancient messages speak directly to contemporary challenges in business ethics, organizational leadership, and personal conduct. Our analysis shows that a speaker's essential character often emerges from just a few simple words, revealing universal truths about the human condition. These biblical insights remain strikingly relevant for modern leaders, offering guidance on servant leadership and the moral foundations for sustainable organizations. Though rooted in antiquity, these messages provide a vital moral compass for navigating the complex ethical terrain of the modern world.

title: Organizational Creativity and Sustainability-oriented Innovation as Drivers of Sustainable Development: Overcoming Firms’ Economic, Environmental, and Social Sustainability Challenges

detail.title: Organizational Creativity and Sustainability-oriented Innovation as Drivers of Sustainable Development: Overcoming Firms’ Economic, Environmental, and Social Sustainability Challenges

keywords: Organizational creativity and sustainability-oriented innovation as drivers of sustainable development: overcoming firms' economic

detail.abstract:
Purpose: Sustainable development is key to firms’ competitiveness, survival, growth, and profitability, although sustainability emerges as a great challenge. The aim of this study is to analyze the links between organizational creativity (which integrates sustainability orientation), sustainability-oriented innovation, and the multidimensionality of firms’ sustainability performance.

Design/methodology/approach: A total of 417 valid responses from manufacturing SMEs were collected through a questionnaire. PLS-SEM is the statistical technique used in the hypothesis testing.

Findings: Organizational creativity (which integrates sustainability orientation) and sustainability-oriented innovation are positively associated with economic sustainability performance, environmental sustainability performance, and social sustainability performance; sustainability-oriented innovation has a partial mediation effect on the relationship between organizational creativity and economic, environmental, and social sustainability performance; and organizational creativity (which integrates sustainability orientation) has a positive effect on sustainability-oriented innovation.

Originality: Sustainability orientation is integrated into organizational creativity without limiting it, sustainability-oriented innovation encompasses innovation and sustainability in all its breadth without forgetting the innovation process openness, and firm’s sustainability performance has a multi-dimensional approach. Such innovation and creativity contribute –in an interconnected way– to sustainable development, as well as overcoming sustainability challenges and firms’ barriers to sustainability. Likewise, the aforementioned creativity must be implemented throughout the company, even beyond its contribution to the innovation process. Thus, the implementation of new ideas, thoughts, perspectives, views, and mental models –fruit of the described creative process– will generate new models and paths in which firms’ profitability, growth and survival are related with overcoming environmental and social problems.

title: Do Policymakers Respond to Science? Evidence from Climate Policy Stringency
affiliations: The University of Hong Kong - Faculty of Business and Economics and The University of Hong Kong - Faculty of Business and Economics

detail.title: Do Policymakers Respond to Science? Evidence from Climate Policy Stringency

publicationDetails.detailsText: HKU Jockey Club Enterprise Sustainability Global Research Institute Paper No. 2026/011
publicationDetails.journalName: Hong Kong University Business School: HKU Jockey Club Enterprise Sustainability Global Research Institute Paper Series

detail.abstract: We study whether policymakers respond to climate science by examining how projected future temperatures affect climate policy stringency. Using temperature projections from 110 coupled ocean-atmosphere general circulation models, we show that regions facing larger projected temperature increases adopt more stringent climate policies. Our identification strategy exploits within-region changes in temperature projections over time that arise from plausibly exogenous improvements in computing power and advances in climate modeling. The positive effect of projected future temperatures on policy stringency is stronger in regions where projections exhibit lower dispersion across models and where public belief in climate change is higher. At the individual level, policymakers with stronger beliefs in climate change are more likely to incorporate climate projections into their voting behavior, whereas age, gender, and education appear to be less relevant.

title: Emerging Technologies and Their Impact on Business Transformation in the United Kingdom

detail.title: Emerging Technologies and Their Impact on Business Transformation in the United Kingdom

detail.abstract:
This research examines the impact of emerging technologies on the global business environment, with a specific focus on blockchain, artificial intelligence (AI), and the Internet of Things (IoT). It explores both the organisational and societal implications of these technologies, providing insights into their practical applications and associated challenges. Blockchain is analysed for its role in transforming financial and transactional systems through innovations such as smart contracts, asset tokenisation, and Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs), which have contributed to increased liquidity and efficiency in traditionally illiquid markets. Real world examples, including the IBM and Maersk TradeLens partnership, are used to illustrate the growing adoption of blockchain solutions.

The study further examines the role of AI in enhancing decision making within multinational organisations, highlighting its capacity to analyse complex data sets, support forecasting and improve strategic planning. Ethical concerns, including bias and transparency in AI driven decision making, are also considered. In addition, the research evaluates the influence of IoT technologies on real time data collection, customer engagement and operational efficiency, particularly through the use of connected devices.

The paper concludes by proposing a strategic framework to address the challenges associated with the adoption of emerging technologies in a global context. Key recommendations include strengthening cybersecurity measures, investing in skills development, ensuring ethical compliance, adopting a customer centric approach, integrating sustainability considerations, and fostering agile strategies and strategic partnerships. These measures are essential for organisations seeking to leverage technological innovation while maintaining competitiveness and long term sustainability in an evolving global marketplace.

title: Venture Capital Contracting as Bargaining in the Shadow of Corporate Law Constraints
affiliations: Bocconi University - Bocconi Law Department,  and Leibniz Institute for Financial Research SAFE

detail.title: Venture Capital Contracting as Bargaining in the Shadow of Corporate Law Constraints

publicationDetails.detailsText: European Corporate Governance Institute - Law Working Paper No. 833/2025
publicationDetails.journalName: European Corporate Governance Institute (ECGI) - Law Working Paper Series
DFG Center for Advanced Studies - Foundations of Law & Finance (LawFin) Working Paper Series
Leibniz Institute for Financial Research SAFE Working Paper Series

detail.abstract:
Venture capital (“VC”) has built a solid reputation for spurring innovation and economic growth, thus emerging as a crown jewel of the U.S. economy since the 1980s. The development of the U.S. VC market has benefited from the enabling nature of U.S. (Delaware) corporate law, which allows parties to devise a complex contractual framework that economists consider the best real-world solution to the market frictions bedeviling the finance of high-tech innovative projects.

The law and finance literature has paid attention to corporate law as one of the determinants of VC investments by examining how variations in shareholder protection shape VC contracting. It has underscored the importance of flexible corporate law to enable the tailor-made arrangements that define VC-backed firms’ unique governance structure. Vice versa, it has also documented anecdotally how mandatory corporate laws can impede the adoption and use of some specific components of the U.S. contractual framework.

This article contributes to this literature, first, by conceptualizing, in a general theoretical framework, the role that flexible or rigid corporate law in action plays in supporting or hindering VC. Second, it identifies the channels through which mandatory corporate law constrains VC contracting. Third, it documents the real-world significance of these phenomena by illustrating how the constraints stemming from the corporate law regimes in force in two European jurisdictions, namely Germany and Italy, impact the transplant of the contractual framework governing VC deals in the U.S.

title: Synthetic Managerial Agents: A Multi-LLM Ensemble Framework for Computational Agent-Based Theory Exploration
affiliations: University of Cambridge, University of Cambridge and University of Sussex Business School

detail.title: Synthetic Managerial Agents: A Multi-LLM Ensemble Framework for Computational Agent-Based Theory Exploration

declarations.funderStatement: Cambridge Trust

detail.abstract: We introduce Synthetic Managerial Agents (SMA), a novel computational methodology that advances agentbased modeling (ABM) by replacing rigid behavioral rules with Large Language Model (LLM)-powered agents capable of flexible theoretical reasoning. Traditional ABM faces a fundamental behavioral specification problem: translating nuanced organizational theories into explicit algorithmic rules strips away the interpretive flexibility that makes theories valuable in practice. SMA addresses this limitation by encoding theoretical frameworks as natural language prompts, enabling agents to reason contextually rather than follow predetermined decision trees. We formalize SMA through a mathematical framework defining agents as tuples A = ⟨S, T, E, D, R⟩ with explicit encoding fidelity assumptions and ensemble robustness properties. The methodology enables theoretical exploration and hypothesis generation,systematically mapping how different theoretical frameworks predict outcomes across varied conditions to identify promising hypotheses for subsequent empirical validation. We demonstrate SMA through two illustrative simulations: market entry decisions across uncertainty levels and team composition across task types. Using ensemble predictions from five LLMs (GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Grok-3, Gemini-2.0-Flash, DeepSeek-V3), we show how LLM-ABM reveals boundary conditions and generates testable hypotheses about theoretical applicability. The methodology achieves three contributions to computational organizational research: (1) solving ABM's behavioral specification problem through natural language theoretical encoding, (2) enabling systematic exploration of theoretical boundary conditions through controlled environmental variation, and (3) providing multiarchitecture validation that distinguishes robust theoretical patterns from model-specific artifacts. SMA positions LLM-powered agents as a methodological complement to traditional ABM and empirical research, generating synthetic data for hypothesis development rather than replacing human-subject studies.

title: The Scaling Paradox of Lifestyle Entrepreneurship: Why Growth Destroys Competitive Advantage
affiliations: University of Cambridge, University of Cambridge, University of Reading - Henley Business School and University of Sussex Business School

detail.title: The Scaling Paradox of Lifestyle Entrepreneurship: Why Growth Destroys Competitive Advantage

declarations.funderStatement: Cambridge Trust

detail.abstract: Does growth help or hurt lifestyle ventures? Conventional wisdom assumes bigger is better, yet we document a scaling paradox: lifestyle entrepreneurship confers survival advantages, but only for small firms. Challenging the deficit view, we find these ventures thrive despite operating with significantly fewer resources. However, this less is more advantage collapses as ventures grow: the operational demands of expansion erode the founder-led authenticity essential for their survival, making growth, rather than resource scarcity, the primary threat. Using data from 1,614 pet industry ventures, we find that lifestyle orientation is positively as- sociated with survival for ventures with fewer than 10 employees (β = +0.049, p = 0.054), but this advantage disappears entirely for larger firms and becomes negative for ventures ex- ceeding 50 employees. The interaction between lifestyle orientation and firm size is strongly significant (β = –0.035, p < 0.01). We theorize that growth destroys the authenticity signals, founder involvement, personal passion, craft-based production, that enable lifestyle ventures to differentiate and build consumer trust. This “scaling paradox” reveals a deeper tension be- tween resources and capabilities: the very capital that enables expansion erodes the founder-led authenticity that attracted investors in the first place. Our findings challenge the growth imper- ative that dominates entrepreneurship research and practice, offering a provocative implication: stay small, stay authentic.

title: The Impact of Dual-agency Leniency Policy on Cartel Detection
affiliations: Yonsei University - Department of Economics and KDI School of Public Policy and Management

detail.title: The Impact of Dual-agency Leniency Policy on Cartel Detection

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: We study cartel detection when two public authorities operate separate leniency programs within the same jurisdiction, as in Korea. We develop a simple repeated-game model to compare single-agency enforcement with dual-agency enforcement, to distinguish independent operation from cooperation, and to examine how the structure of leniency relief affects reporting incentives. When the two programs operate independently and do not recognize each other's leniency status, firms may have weaker incentives to self-report, and reporting can become concentrated in only one program. Cooperation that recognizes leniency rank across authorities restores a race to report and can make self-reporting attractive under a broader range of enforcement environments. The analysis also shows that cooperation is most reliable when early applicants receive comparable treatment across authorities: when second-in-line relief is available only in the administrative program, stronger criminal exposure can reduce the effectiveness of cooperation by raising the residual risk borne by non-first applicants. The policy implication is that effective dual-agency leniency can be achieved through a narrow form of coordination that verifies marker status and aligns the relief structure across authorities while preserving confidentiality.

title: Gaza and the Ethics of Contemporary War: Siege, Civilian Harm, and Moral Evasion

detail.title: Gaza and the Ethics of Contemporary War: Siege, Civilian Harm, and Moral Evasion

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no financial or personal relationships that could be construed as a potential conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This research does not involve human subjects, human participants, or private personal data. As a theoretical and analytical study based on publicly available sources and philosophical analysis, it did not require institutional ethics approval.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding and was independently conducted by the author.

detail.abstract: Gaza has become one of the most visible sites of contemporary armed conflict, yet its ethical significance is often obscured by the intensity of political debate surrounding it. This paper treats Gaza not as an exceptional moral spectacle, but as a structural test case for contemporary war ethics. It examines how siege warfare, civilian exposure, and prolonged insecurity persist alongside extensive legal, humanitarian, and moral discourse, raising questions about the capacity of existing ethical frameworks to interrupt foreseeable harm. Drawing on the concept of moral drift developed in earlier work, the paper analyzes how international humanitarian law, proportionality reasoning, securitization, and moral exceptionalism interact to normalize civilian suffering without requiring overt norm violation. Ethical language remains active, but its function shifts from constraint to management. Civilian harm is acknowledged, assessed, and narrated, yet rarely allowed to function as a decisive moral limit. By examining siege conditions, cumulative harm, and the temporal endurance of violence, the paper argues that Gaza illustrates a broader pattern in contemporary warfare: ethical frameworks persist rhetorically while losing their interruptive force. The paper concludes by reaffirming a consequence-centered ethical orientation, in which foreseeable and sustained civilian harm must become morally decisive rather than administratively tolerable. Gaza, in this sense, is not an anomaly, but a lens through which the ethical limits of modern war are made visible.

title: Production Planning Optimization: Going One Step Ahead of Economic Order Quantity Model
affiliations: University of Southern California, Marshall School of Business, Students

detail.title: Production Planning Optimization: Going One Step Ahead of Economic Order Quantity Model
detail.abstract: Economic Order Quantity employs higher order quantities which lead to surplus inventory resulting in increased total cost. Due to this, there is a constraint that manufacturing houses and production planners face, which somehow reduces their competencies to respond to demand variability. In this case, one uses a powerful solver in an Open Solver platform that utilizes Gurobi Engine for solving complex problems using the Linear Optimization principle. The EOQ model uses higher total capacity than the Open Solver which means that resource optimization is on the higher side with the production planning optimization model. EOQ doesn't consider seasonality factor as much as it is anticipated in the production planning as the minimum inventory doesn't consider management of lot size as per the demand. The open solver model has the capability to optimize not only the inventory handling costs but also the overtime cost of the labor which drastically decreases the labor costs. To represent certain intricacies on how the model provides an optimal output over EOQ with different scenarios based on a simple "What-if" criteria will explain about the parameters ranging from the sourcing to the manufacturing of two products as a pilot test. Also, the model will give the insight to inspect how certain decision parameters have overarching effects on the entire production planning process. Furthermore, it can be expected that the Forecast Accuracy can lead to the formulation of this planning process by considering the minimum inventory WeeksCover (Weeks of Supply) and calculating the total savings throughout the time.

title: Do U.S. Sanctions Significantly Impact the Financing Constraints of Chinese-listed Firms?
affiliations: Central University of Finance and Economics, Shenzhen University,  and Department of Accounting and Corporate Governance

detail.title: Do U.S. Sanctions Significantly Impact the Financing Constraints of Chinese-listed Firms?
detail.abstract: This study examines whether U.S. sanctions significantly impact the financing constraints of Chinese listed firms. Using a uniquely constructed dataset of Chinese A-share firms spanning the 2007 to 2021 period that were directly impacted by the U.S. sanctions, we provide strong evidence showing a positive relationship between sanctions and financing constraints. Additional analyses indicate that the positive relationship between sanctions and financing constraints is more (less) pronounced for firms with greater risk exposure (strong market position, strong innovation and research capabilities, and effective government support policies). Sanctions also increase the financing costs for affected firms, shorten their financing duration, and complicate their access to financing. Finally, various endogeneity tests and robustness checks confirm our baseline results. Overall, our study provides important insights into the detrimental effect of U.S. sanctions on Chinese firms' financing constraints.

title: Liquid Staking and the Limits of Policy
affiliations: University of Oxford - Oxford-Man Institute of Quantitative Finance, Stevens Institute of Technology - School of Business and Imperial College Business School

detail.title: Liquid Staking and the Limits of Policy
detail.abstract: We study the role of liquid staking and how it affects the  interaction between issuance policy, economic productivity, and security in proof-of-stake blockchains, with a focus on the role of liquid staking. In a dynamic macro-finance framework, we show that issuance redistributes resources from productive on-chain activity to validators, which effectively acts as a tax on productive capital. This mechanism generates a Laffer-curve-type tradeoff: beyond an interior optimum, higher issuance weakens the productive base that finances security and reduces staking rewards. We then introduce liquid staking, which allows users to earn staking rewards while retaining liquidity for productive use. Liquid staking collapses the traditional tradeoff between staking and DeFi. When liquid staking tokens (LSTs) closely substitute for the native asset and benefit from strategic complementarities, issuance reallocates productive activity toward LSTs, compresses the feasible policy space, and can render issuance and slashing ineffective as policy instruments.

title: Abuse Abroad: Torture, Detention, Occupation, and the Moral Collapse of U.S. Power

detail.title: Abuse Abroad: Torture, Detention, Occupation, and the Moral Collapse of U.S. Power

declarations.ethicsApproval: This research does not involve human subjects, human participants, or private personal data. As a theoretical and analytical study based on publicly available sources and philosophical analysis, it did not require institutional ethics approval.

detail.abstract: This paper examines torture, detention, and occupation as institutional instruments of power within the United States' military and counterterrorism campaigns in the Middle East, rejecting narratives that frame abuse as aberrational, reactive, or the result of individual misconduct. Drawing on international political ethics, human rights law, critical security studies, and social psychology, the analysis demonstrates how systems of coercion were deliberately designed, legally narrated, and culturally justified in ways that enabled widespread physical, psychological, and moral harm. Torture is treated not as an episodic violation, but as a predictable outcome of institutional structures built around secrecy, exceptionalism, and dehumanization. The paper situates U.S. practices within broader patterns of Islamophobia, racialized threat construction, and moral exceptionalism, tracing continuities from pre-9/11 surveillance and profiling through post-9/11 detention regimes, occupation governance, and contemporary policies such as the Muslim ban. It argues that the persistence of abuse despite its absolute prohibition reveals a profound ethical failure rooted in power preservation rather than security necessity. This paper is written with an explicit moral purpose. It is offered as a formal ethical apology, by a U.S.-born citizen, to the individuals and communities harmed by American military, political, and institutional actions across the Middle East. The apology does not seek absolution or closure; it seeks acknowledgment, accountability, and refusal. By centering consequence over justification, the paper calls for a reorientation of political ethics away from domination and toward moral responsibility for sustained harm.

title: Following the Quiet Call: Reflections on Vocation and Faith

detail.title: Following the Quiet Call: Reflections on Vocation and Faith
detail.abstract:
This article presents an autoethnographic reflection on vocational discernment, drawing from personal experiences spanning several decades. It explores how God’s call unfolds gradually through interior movements, lived experiences, relational guidance, and reflective attention to the heart’s deepest desires. Drawing from experiences in attraction to religious life, exploration of marriage, years of professional work, periods of spiritual dryness, subconscious reflection through dreams, and engagement in spiritual mentoring, the essay identifies key vocational signs that shaped discernment. 

These signs include desire, attraction, environment, personal values, marriage considerations, life events and circumstances, influence of other people, inner conviction, ordinary prayer, unexpected promptings, ordinary listening, and realism. Findings suggest that vocation is realized through sustained peace, perseverance, and interior growth, and that discernment is an ongoing process, nurtured by accompaniment, reflection, and attentive responsiveness to both subtle and ordinary indicators of God’s call. 

The article highlights that vocation is not a momentary clarity but a lifelong journey in which everyday life, relationships, and interior movements become formative spaces for responding to God’s invitation.

title: Firm Dynamics, Inflation, and the Transmission of Monetary Policy
affiliations: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

detail.title: Firm Dynamics, Inflation, and the Transmission of Monetary Policy

publicationDetails.detailsText: Finance and Economics Discussion Series, issue 2026-003, 2026[10.17016/FEDS.2026.003]

publicationDetails.journalName: Board of Governors: Finance & Economics Discussion Series (Topic)

detail.abstract: I study how fluctuations in business formation and destruction affect inflation and the transmission of monetary policy. To do this analysis, I extend a New Keynesian model to include endogenous business formation and destruction and heterogeneous producers. A decline in the number of producers puts upward pressure on inflation, and I find that this mechanism can explain about half of the missing deflation following the Great Recession. I then study the transmission of monetary policy in this framework. I show that endogenous fluctuations in entry generate an intertemporal trade-off in monetary policy; a contractionary shock leads employment and inflation to decline on impact, but inflation later overshoots, as the shock also causes a decline in entry and an increase in exit.

title: Digital Knowledge Stratification: A Socio-Legal Analysis of Technological Redlining and the Right to Education for Syrian Youth

detail.title: Digital Knowledge Stratification: A Socio-Legal Analysis of Technological Redlining and the Right to Education for Syrian Youth
detail.abstract: This research explores the intersection of international sanctions regimes and digital rights, focusing on the phenomenon of “technological redlining” experienced by Syrian youth. Using a qualitative phenomenological approach, the paper examines how corporate over-compliance by global technology providers hinders access to education, as protected under Article 13 of the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (ICESCR). Through the lived experiences of three individuals, the study highlights the human cost of digital exclusion, arguing that equitable access to knowledge is essential for personal and societal development. It contrasts the legal provisions of “General Licenses” with the restrictive “Terms of Service” enforced by private actors. The research concludes with a proposal for a “Digital Humanitarian Corridor” and a “Global Academic Passport” to mitigate the growing divide in global knowledge access.

title: Abnormal Returns following Business Model Extensions -The Role of Demand Relatedness
affiliations: WU Vienna University of Economics and Business and Vienna University of Economics and Business

detail.title: Abnormal Returns following Business Model Extensions -The Role of Demand Relatedness
detail.abstract: This article explores the impact of business model extensions (BMEs) on company performance by distinguishing between demand-related (BME-DR) and demand-unrelated (BME-DU) extensions. We explain that BME-DRs can enhance customer utility and, thus, drive firm performance. Furthermore, we hypothesize that a negative business outlook and the degree of diversification are important moderators of the BME-DR-performance relationship. We use an event study methodology to substantiate this claim and analyze abnormal returns following BME announcements. This approach allows us to precisely measure market reactions to announcements of BME-DR and BME-DU. Our findings reveal that BME-DRs lead to higher abnormal stock market returns than BME-DU. Moreover, companies with a pessimistic business outlook disproportionately benefit from BME-DRs. Finally, contrary to our hypothesis, we find that the benefits of BME-DRs do not uniformly accrue. Rather, the relationship between diversification and the effectiveness of such extensions follows an inverted U-shaped pattern, suggesting limited benefits for minimally and highly diversified firms. We discuss these findings and conclude that, beyond a certain level of overall company diversification, the cost of managing added complexity outweighs the benefits of BME-DRs.

title: Retention strategies and predictors of retention for longitudinal observational cohort studies: A scoping review
affiliations: Seoul National University - College of Medicine, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Harvard University

detail.title: Retention strategies and predictors of retention for longitudinal observational cohort studies: A scoping review
detail.abstract: ObjectivesParticipant retention is key to generating meaningful findings in longitudinal research studies. Previous systematic reviews have identified strategies for increasing participant retention. This scoping review examines recent innovations in methodology used for participant retention and representation to inform retention practices in the All of Us Research Program (AoU).MethodsThree databases (PubMed, Embase, and CINAHL) were searched for recent studies to include in the literature review. Landmark longitudinal cohort studies were manually selected and searched on study websites and PubMed. AoU archive materials were identified on the AoU Confluence platform that stores internal study resources. Data on retention strategies were extracted, categorized according to retention themes identified in the systematic reviews by Robinson et al. (2015) and Teague et al. (2018), and summarized. Additional data on predictors of retention, digital retention methods, and new retention strategies were also extracted and narratively synthesized.ResultsTwenty-two longitudinal observational studies, 10 landmark cohort studies, and materials from 28 sites in the 14 AoU consortia met inclusion criteria. Contact and scheduling methods, visit characteristics, and special tracking methods were the most common retention themes used among the three data sources. Disability and lack of healthcare access were associated with lower odds of retention, whereas higher education and older age were associated with higher odds of retention. Digital strategies mostly involved the use of study websites, social media platforms, and digital tools to conduct follow-up, contact participants, or track participant information. The most common new strategies that were not included in previous reviews were retention committees, staff meetings on retention, and check-in calls. Segmentation approaches were identified as a new retention theme, including retention call lists and participant segmentation to individualize retention.ConclusionsThis scoping review reports on current methods used to retain participants in recent literature, landmark longitudinal cohort studies, and AoU archive materials. The review identified recent progress in the development and implementation of participant retention practices, as well as gaps in research assessing the effectiveness of specific retention strategies on increasing retention rates among different demographics, especially those who are underrepresented in biomedical research (UBR).

title: Strengthening Public-Private Partnerships in Bangladesh: Institutional Challenges and Strategic Reforms for Vision 2041

detail.title: Strengthening Public-Private Partnerships in Bangladesh: Institutional Challenges and Strategic Reforms for Vision 2041

detail.abstract: Bangladesh's path to upper-middle-income status by 2041 hinges on transformative infrastructure expansion, with annual investment needs estimated at USD 10-12 billion. Conventional public financing mechanisms are insufficient to meet this demand, especially as external aid flows decline in the post-LDC transition. This paper positions Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) not as a supplementary tool, but as a strategic imperative for bridging fiscal gaps, mobilizing private capital, and accelerating infrastructure delivery across transport, energy, and urban services. Building on global PPP models and Bangladesh's policy evolution since 2010, the paper reviews frameworks from the UK, Australia, India, and China, and examines domestic challenges through reports and field-level experience. It incorporates practitioner insights from the author's roles in the Bangladesh Economic Zones Authority (BEZA), the Dhaka Bypass Expressway, and the Planning Commission. The paper uses a mixed-method approach combining document analysis, comparative case studies, and implementation experience to highlight the need for bankable project design, transparent procurement, and inclusive governance. It contributes to the policy discourse on development financing and institutional reform, offering strategic recommendations for policymakers, development partners, and civil society. It also shows how PPPs can advance key Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), including clean energy, decent work, innovation, and urban resilience.

title: Disputation on the Power and Efficiency of Representative Bureaucracy Debating Future Research Agendas
affiliations: American University

detail.title: Disputation on the Power and Efficiency of Representative Bureaucracy Debating Future Research Agendas
detail.abstract: In the tradition of Martin Luther posting 95 theses for debate on indulgences and related church issues, this papers offers 41 critical issues for debate in the literature on representative bureaucracy. 2 While they do not constitute a unified theory or theology of representative bureaucracy, they raise critical issues about the potential of representative bureaucracy to explain some key elements related to the role of bureaucracy in democratic governance and warn of pitfalls that will detract from key issues to less important theoretical/theological points.

title: From Tulip to Gold: Rational Bubbles in Consumable Assets
affiliations: Seoul National University - College of Business Administration and Amsterdam Business School, University of Amsterdam

detail.title: From Tulip to Gold: Rational Bubbles in Consumable Assets
detail.abstract: We study bubble dynamics when the speculative object is also a consumption good. We build an overlapping-generations model in which a storable asset can be held as a store of value or consumed for direct utility, making aggregate inventory (and effective float) central to pricing. The model yields two insights: (i) even small consumption value anchors resale prices to a consumption outside option, disciplining bubble indeterminacy and sharpening equilibrium selection; and (ii) fluctuations in "use" value trigger discrete, state-dependent reductions in circulating supply, producing sharp price moves around burn/bind/redeem events and tying bubbles to scarcity. We extend the framework to endogenous, costly issuance, generating feedback among prices, speculative demand, utility, and quantity. The model offers a unified lens for bubbles in storable commodities and in digital assets such as cryptocurrencies, tokens, and in-platform collectibles.

title: Productivity and Quality of Multi-product Firms
affiliations: University of Trento - School of International Studies, UNSW Business School and University of New South Wales - School of Economics

detail.title: Productivity and Quality of Multi-product Firms

publicationDetails.journalName: Board of Governors: International Finance Discussion Papers (Topic)

detail.abstract: This paper introduces a method for estimating productivity and quality at the firm-product level using a transformation function framework. We use firm optimization conditions to establish a one-to-one mapping between observed data and unobserved productivity and quality. We do not need to impute firm-product input shares and can avoid imposing productivity evolution processes. The method is scalable to numerous products and can address the bias caused by unobserved heterogeneous intermediate input prices. We apply the method to a set of Mexican manufacturing industries and examine the roles of across-firm and within-firm technological spillovers, accounting for the trade-off between productivity and quality. Our quantitative analysis shows that an exogenous, product-specific technological improvement generates substantial gains in welfare, amplified by both within-firm and across-firm spillovers by approximately 17 percent and 5 percent, respectively. Moreover, within-firm resource reallocation toward the most productive products accounts for 60 percent of the resulting firm-level productivity gains.

title: Social Learning as a Microfoundation of Digital Entrepreneurial Ecosystems: Evidence from Decentralized Autonomous Organizations (DAOs)
affiliations: Technische Universität München (TUM) and Syracuse University - Whitman School of Management

detail.title: Social Learning as a Microfoundation of Digital Entrepreneurial Ecosystems: Evidence from Decentralized Autonomous Organizations (DAOs)
detail.abstract: We identify a core microfoundation of digital entrepreneurial ecosystems (EE): social learning in the form of information cascades. Using decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs) as a laboratory where micro-level coordination processes are directly observable on blockchains, we trace how individual-level voting behavior aggregates into ecosystem-level outcomes. Exploring hand-collected data covering 19,450,710 votes from 924,095 unique voters in 3,317 DAO governance proposals, we estimate economically strong information cascades that run from influential through early to late voters. Several contextual factors impede social learning in DAOs, including the presence of cybercriminals in the DAO community and market sentiment, while the decentralization of token ownership is an important prerequisite for information cascades to unfold. Finally, we document a link between the potency of information cascades and the financial performance of DAOs. Stronger information cascades are associated with higher market capitalization, trading volume, and abnormal cryptocurrency token returns. Overall, we contribute to the EE literature by demonstrating how observable micro-level learning processes triggered by influential agents in the network scale into ecosystem-level financial performance.

title: A Distributional Sensitivity Engine: Greeks from Two-Measure Digital Weights and Conditional Law Blocks

detail.title: A Distributional Sensitivity Engine: Greeks from Two-Measure Digital Weights and Conditional Law Blocks
detail.abstract: BSM Sensitivity Engine (BSE) derives a compact, implementation-oriented representation for first-and mixed second-order sensitivities of the Black-Scholes-Merton (BSM) price by differentiating with respect to an arbitrary scalar parameter and organizing the chain-rule terms into universal weights together with a single "weight-motion" correction channel. Distributional Sensitivity Engine (DSE) extends this engine viewpoint beyond the closed-form BSM setting for equity diffusions with deterministic term structures by rewriting the in-the-money event using a Doleans-Dade exponential of the stochastic integral and an associated Girsanov change of measure. Under the exponential-martingale condition (Appendix E) and the differentiation/regularity assumptions (Appendix F), the time-t price admits a two-weight form V_t=w_1 a_1+w_2 a_2 with F_t-measurable prefactors (a_1,a_2) and conditional "digital" weights under Q and Q^+. Differentiating this representation yields a four-input first-derivative engine V_(t,x)=∑_(k=1)^4 w_k  a_(k,x) whose weights depend only on conditional CDF/PDF blocks of the Doleans-Dade log variable E_(t,T) under the two measures. Mixed partials retain the same structure as in BSE: a dot product between common weights and second derivatives of primitives plus an explicit correction channel that collects products of first derivatives induced by weight dependence. This correction admits a matrix/Jacobian representation in terms of distributional Jacobian/Hessian blocks, providing an implementation-ready recipe once the conditional CDF/PDF blocks (and their parameter derivatives) are supplied by a numerical backend. In the deterministic-volatility BSM specialization these blocks reduce to normal CDF/PDF objects and the framework recovers the BSE Γ/vanna/volga-identified decomposition, providing closed-form regression targets for verification. The resulting separation of deterministic primitives from a probabilistic core suggests modular PDE or Monte Carlo implementations for the distributional blocks while keeping the sensitivity logic unchanged.

title: High-Frequency Trading and Price Discovery: The Role of Strategic Runs
affiliations: Goethe University Frankfurt

detail.title: High-Frequency Trading and Price Discovery: The Role of Strategic Runs
detail.abstract: Strategic runs are an outcome of high-frequency trading strategies that lead to alternating cycles of order submissions and cancellations within a short time interval. Examining granular limit order book data, we find that submissions and cancellations resulting from these runs have less permanent price impact and contribute less to price discovery than similar trading activities not part of a strategic run. Once other market participants can recognize that an order belongs to a strategic run, its contribution to price discovery diminishes significantly. Our findings indicate that such high-frequency trading activities do not enhance price discovery but rather dilute it by triggering a substantial number of orders with limited informational value.

title: The Future Of Risk Is Predictive

detail.title: The Future Of Risk Is Predictive
detail.abstract: Delivered as the Riskonet Webinar on the 29th January 2026, the presentation launches the discussion on the top global and local risks for 2026. It asserts that the whilst the global top risk can be summarised as geopolitical instability with cascading economic and climate consequences and the local top risk as state fragility manifesting as infrastructure failure and governance breakdown, that in practice, the real global risk is the systemic breakdown across borders where shocks cascade faster that we can respond. It proposes that without the use of predictive tools, the speed at which risks manifest will continue to be a blind spot and weaken risk processes due to the increased complexity of today's risks environment.

title: The Political Economy of Natural Resources in the Caspian Sea region: Challenges for Transitions to Democracy
affiliations: Economic Research Center (ERC)

detail.title: The Political Economy of Natural Resources in the Caspian Sea region: Challenges for Transitions to Democracy
detail.abstract:
The political economy of natural resources[1] is not a new area of study, but focusing on the Caspian Basin countries, in particular, is a less-researched angle.  In this paper, I focus on three countries in the Caspian Sea region: Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, and Russia. While I had hoped also to consider the cases of Turkmenistan and Iran, there were problems with access to information for both countries.

A distinguishing feature of this article is my discussion of the significant role that the Caspian Sea region plays on the global stage. In particular, Russia’s recent aggression and attempt to change the political and administrative structure of the region, has garnered the attention of policymakers and researchers around the world. This paper will seek to evaluate the possible outcome of Russia’s actions in the region, as well as subsequent implications.

In this paper, I also attempt to estimate the result of falling oil prices and its impact on the behaviors of decision-makers and business people. The current economic context will therefore create new and interesting behavioral trends for further research and analysis.


[1] The political economy of natural resources[1] is means how natural assets affect the political system.

reference: Richard D. Pomp, A Second Bite at the Apple, a Hail Mary, and a Rush to Judgment, 188 Tax Notes 767 (2025).
title: A Second Bite at the Apple, a Hail Mary, And a Rush to Judgment
affiliations: University of Connecticut - School of Law

detail.title: A Second Bite at the Apple, a Hail Mary, And a Rush to Judgment

publicationDetails.detailsText: Richard D. Pomp, A Second Bite at the Apple, a Hail Mary, and a Rush to Judgment, 188 Tax Notes 767 (2025).

detail.abstract:
In this article, Professor Pomp responds to recent commentary defending Maryland’s digital advertising tax against challenges under the Internet Tax Freedom Act’s (ITFA) nondiscrimination clause. He seeks to correct the record based on the evidence presented in recent Maryland Tax Court proceedings involving Peacock, Apple, and Google.

Maryland’s digital advertising tax is defended on the premise that online advertising is not similar to offline advertising, and thus does not violate ITFA’s nondiscrimination clause. This position hinges on a unique and unusual definition of digital advertising that appears neither in the Maryland statute nor anywhere else. The trial record shows that this definition was rejected under cross-examination, unsupported by industry or authoritative sources, and inconsistent with the state’s expert’s prior work. The state’s subsequent technical bulletin adopting that definition represents a bootstrap effort to obtain deference for last minute testimony.

The Internet Tax Freedom Act’s nondiscrimination prohibition is designed to provide broad protection for electronic commerce and, therefore, must be interpreted at a level of generality that focuses on substance rather than form. Whether online and offline advertising differ in technology, efficiency, or method of delivery is irrelevant; for purposes of discrimination analysis, “advertising is advertising.” A granular approach that emphasizes the form of the advertising is a narrow, granular approach with the result that online taxable advertising will almost never be comparable to offline exempt advertising, thereby rendering ITFA’s nondiscrimination clause meaningless.

Members of Congress understood that electronic commerce would be faster, better, more efficient, and nimbler than offline activity. They sought to avoid built-in obsolescence in a rapidly changing field. ITFA was enacted to foster, encourage, and safeguard anticipated innovations. It was not meant to allow states to use these very differences between online and offline commerce to justify discrimination. A granular, form-based approach flips ITFA on its head. It allows discrimination to be justified by the very innovations Congress sought to protect. It also invites ad hoc, fact-bound litigation in an advertising ecosystem where practices can change hourly or daily.

The article concludes that statutory interpretation and tax policy require a substance-based framework that compares taxable online and exempt offline advertising by their shared function: communicating a message to an audience. Treating all advertising services alike offers consistency, predictability, administrability, and protects reliance interests for states and taxpayers. This approach upholds Congress’s goal of ensuring a “tax-fair internet, not a tax-free one.”

title: Kantian Time as a Quantum Continuum: Structural Constraints in the Transcendental Aesthetic
affiliations: Newcastle University

detail.title: Kantian Time as a Quantum Continuum: Structural Constraints in the Transcendental Aesthetic

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No interests of conflict.
declarations.ethicsApproval: No ethical statement required.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding.

detail.abstract:
Kant's doctrine of time in the Critique of Pure Reason treats time as the pure form of inner sense and an a priori condition for representing succession, while denying that it is an object, a magnitude, or a feature of things in themselves. This combination of claims raises a structural problem. How can time be continuous, unified, and infinitely divisible without being reified or assimilated to a mathematical or physical continuum? 

This paper addresses that problem by offering a minimal axiomatic reconstruction of Kantian time using order-theoretic tools. Kant's core claims are captured by a small set of structural constraints governing a strict temporal order and a formal indexing of appearances. From these constraints, the paper derives both familiar Kantian results, such as the absence of first and last moments and the unity of temporal succession, and further consequences, including the exclusion of cyclical and branching temporal orders and the absence of intrinsic structure at temporal positions.

Under a natural regulative assumption concerning the finitude of appear- ances, the resulting temporal order admits an order-isomorphism with the rational line (Q, <). This result is diagnostic rather than classificatory. It shows that the continuity required for temporal awareness depends on density rather than metric completeness. Kantian time thus emerges as structurally continuous but ontologically thin, clarifying its distinctive position in debates about temporal continuity, structure, and idealism.

title: Neo-Schumpeterian Growth: Political and Religious Stability Matter
affiliations: ,  and Independent

detail.title: Neo-Schumpeterian Growth: Political and Religious Stability Matter

keywords: OECD members and candidates panel O30

detail.abstract: The purpose of this paper is to re-investigate one of the most prominent predictions of Neo-Schumpeterian growth theory-namely, that economic development is augmented by investments in R&D-by stressing that such a prediction applies only when conditional on institutional and sociocultural stability. To achieve this aim, an unbalanced panel data set of 23 OECD members and accession candidate countries from 1998 to 2018 is employed to estimate a Type III growth equation extended by interaction terms between R&D intensity and government/religious stability. Using a full set of macro controls and country-specific fixed effects, it is found that the marginal association of R&D and economic development strictly increases with institutional stability. Quantitatively, a 1-standard-deviation increase in R&D intensity is found to have a negligible association with GDP per capita when government stability is low but raises GDP per capita by up to 13.3% when government stability is high. Moreover, a symmetric relation is found such that a 1-standard-deviation increase in R&D intensity raises GDP per capita by up to 12.9% when religious stability is high. In contrast, the unconditional association between R&D and economic development is found to be small and statistically indistinguishable from zero when religious stability is low.

title: Trade Policy Uncertainty and Trade in the Short Run: An Empirical Investigation of the Reciprocal Tariff

detail.title: Trade Policy Uncertainty and Trade in the Short Run: An Empirical Investigation of the Reciprocal Tariff
detail.abstract: This paper examines the short run effects of trade policy uncertainty (TPU) arising from the U.S. Reciprocal Tariff announcement. Using monthly import data, we find that U.S. firms increased imports from countries facing higher TPU. Contrary to conventional views that TPU suppresses trade, our results highlight a distinct short run importer response consistent with recent inventory management theories. This study offers one of the first empirical assessments of the Reciprocal Tariff's impact and contributes to understanding how firms react to trade policy uncertainty in the short term.

title: TECH GIANT EXCLUSION
affiliations: Seattle University School of Law

detail.title: TECH GIANT EXCLUSION
detail.abstract: There is no topic in regulatory policy that is more pressing and more controversial than what to do about the tech giants-Google, Facebook, Amazon, and Apple. Critics claim that these powerful platforms crush competitors, distort the political process, and elude antitrust law because the law cares only about consumer prices. The only solution, critics argue, is to break them up. The tech giants have indeed engaged in anticompetitive conduct. They have excluded rivals selling products on their platforms by demoting them in search results, copying their products, or refusing to deal with them. While these tactics have harmed consumers, they have never been successfully challenged because they have rarely, if ever, created monopoly power or a dangerous probability of monopoly power, which the Sherman Act requires. This requirement should be eliminated. The tech giants should not be broken up. Splitting them into smaller versions of themselves would result in higher prices or lower quality. Preventing them from selling their own products on their platforms would deprive consumers of choices they value. Nor should the goals of antitrust law be changed. The fundamental aim of antitrust law is to protect consumers and vulnerable suppliers-such as workers-from anticompetitive conduct. If courts also had to focus on preserving small business and limiting the political influence of large firms, the goals of antitrust would conflict. Courts would have no objective way of resolving the conflict, the rule of law would suffer, and consumers and workers would be hurt. Congress should instead amend the Sherman Act to prohibit exclusionary conduct that significantly reduces competition, whether or not it results in actual or probable monopoly power. To avoid chilling procompetitive conduct, the change should apply only to the tech giants and should contain strict proof requirements. This careful expansion would make it much easier to deter tech giant exclusion that harms consumers or workers.

reference: Central Bank of Ireland Research Paper Series No. 1
title: Do Non-Bank Lenders Mitigate Credit Supply Shocks? Evidence from a Major Bank Exit
affiliations: , University College Dublin (UCD) and

detail.title: Do Non-Bank Lenders Mitigate Credit Supply Shocks? Evidence from a Major Bank Exit

publicationDetails.detailsText: Central Bank of Ireland Research Paper Series No. 1
publicationDetails.journalName: Central Bank of Ireland Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We study the transmission of credit supply shocks to firms by exploiting the unexpected exit of the third-largest lender in the Irish business lending market in 2020 and a unique matched firm-lender dataset that covers both banks and nonbank financial institutions. We find that borrowers of the exiting bank receive less credit along both the extensive and intensive margin in the period after the announcement, highlighting that credit supply is not perfectly substitutable across lenders. However, we show that this negative credit supply shock is partly mitigated by non-bank lenders. Borrowers of the exiting bank are more likely to borrow from non-banks following the shock, with the effects driven by business loan facilities, and stronger among riskier firms.

reference: Indian Economic Journal, Special Issue, 1 B, December, 2025, pp.946-957.
title: Marketing the Sustainability Initiatives in India: The Status of Green-House Gas Emissions (GHGs) and the Carbon Market
affiliations: Rashtrasant Tukadoji Maharaj Nagpur University

detail.title: Marketing the Sustainability Initiatives in India: The Status of Green-House Gas Emissions (GHGs) and the Carbon Market

publicationDetails.detailsText: Indian Economic Journal, Special Issue, 1 B, December, 2025, pp.946-957.

detail.abstract: This study examines domestic and international efforts to market sustainability initiatives by examining the state of GHG emissions and the development of the carbon market, with a particular emphasis on India. International accords, starting with the 1972 Stockholm Conference and ending with the legally binding emission reduction targets set by the Kyoto Protocol (1997), were prompted by global concerns over resource overuse and ensuing climate shifts. The Emissions Trading System (ETS), Clean Development Mechanism (CDM), and Joint Implementation (JI) are the three crucial market-based mechanisms that were developed by the Protocol to solve environmental market failure by internalizing the societal cost of pollution. By creating Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) and mandating that all parties, especially developing countries, commit to aggressive carbon reduction targets, the ensuing 2015 Paris Agreement solidified this direction. An analysis of India's industrial landscape's Global Warming Potentials (GWP) between 2005 and 2018 shows alarming patterns, including an almost universal increase across industries. Importantly, GWP increases of more than 268% were recorded in sectors like Non-Ferrous Metals, Other Energy Industries, and Chemicals & Fertilizers. With 36 nations implementing ETS and 39 enacting national carbon taxes, the use of carbon pricing schemes has increased globally. But taken as a whole, these tools only account for 24% of world emissions. Although the European Union ETS is the largest compliance market in the world, major compliance markets such as China and New Zealand saw substantial price fluctuation in the early months of 2025, which raised concerns about the stability and effectiveness of the market. By tokenizing carbon credits and turning them into digital assets on block chain systems, as demonstrated by exchanges like Toucan Protocol, the industry is also seeing technological advancement. India has introduced the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS), 2023 in accordance with its NDC pledge to reduce carbon emissions by 45% by 2030 (compared to 2005 levels) and achieve net-zero emissions by 2070. The Grid Controller of India (GCI) and the Central Electrical Regulatory Commission (CERC) oversee registry and trade operations, respectively, while the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) administers the CCTS. National carbon neutrality programs that concentrate on afforestation, clean air projects, and the creation of Carbon Capture Utilization and Storage (CCUS) frameworks to alleviate the industry's excessive reliance on coal are employed in conjunction with these efforts. The paper advocates for a community-involved, government-regulated system for the payment and control of CO2 emitters, arguing that a more comprehensive and effective regulation model may need to go beyond merely market-oriented measures in order to assure true sustainability.

reference: Bank of Italy Occasional Paper No. 959
title: Macroeconomic Surprises and Financial Market Reactions: Insights into Euro-Area Interest Rates
affiliations: Bank of Italy and Imperial College Business School

detail.title: Macroeconomic Surprises and Financial Market Reactions: Insights into Euro-Area Interest Rates

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Italy Occasional Paper No. 959
publicationDetails.journalName: Bank of Italy Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper examines how euro-area (EA) interest rates react to EA and US macroeconomic surprises. We find that the sensitivity of interest rates to surprises varies across tenors and over time. Short-term OIS rates are significantly less sensitive to macroeconomic surprises than longer-term rates. During the forward guidance period (2013-22), interest rate reactivity was rather muted, especially at the short end of the yield curve. Term premia accounted almost entirely for the sensitivity observed at the long end of the curve. Since the ECB’s adoption of a data-dependent and meeting-by-meeting approach, interest rate sensitivity has forcefully surged back to the levels observed during the Great Financial Crisis. In particular, EA OIS rates have become highly sensitive to US surprises, thus pointing to significant spillovers from US economic developments to EA financial conditions. Monetary policy uncertainty amplifies the sensitivity of interest rates to surprises, especially to those related to US economic developments and for the expected short term rate component.

reference: Bank of Italy Occasional Paper No. 957
title: The Economic Impact of European Capital Market Integration
affiliations: Bank of Italy, Bank of Italy, Bank of Italy, Bank of Italy and Bank of Italy

detail.title: The Economic Impact of European Capital Market Integration

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Italy Occasional Paper No. 957
publicationDetails.journalName: Bank of Italy Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Enhancing innovation and productivity is a primary challenge for the European economy. To achieve this goal, it is essential to step up investment in innovative projects. Advancing the integration of capital markets, a key objective of the Savings and Investment Union, can be pivotal in this effort by reducing financing costs and strengthening the investment ecosystem. We argue that the integration of European capital markets – including the introduction of a common European safe asset – could raise investment levels by approximately 1 per cent of GDP. Over a ten-year horizon this would raise GDP by 1.5 per cent. If additional investment were focused on R&D spending, the impact would be three times as great.

reference: World Affairs: The Journal of International Issues, Volume 29, No. 03. Pp. 38-61, 2025
title: The Iran-Israel War of 2025: A Catalyst for Human Rights Crisis and Global Order Reconfiguration
affiliations: Aligarh Muslim University and Aligarh Muslim University (AMU)

detail.title: The Iran-Israel War of 2025: A Catalyst for Human Rights Crisis and Global Order Reconfiguration

publicationDetails.detailsText: World Affairs: The Journal of International Issues, Volume 29, No. 03. Pp. 38-61, 2025

detail.abstract: The Iran-Israel War of 2025 marks a historic rupture in Middle Eastern geopolitics, transitioning from covert proxy confrontations to overt stateto-state warfare. This article explores how the conflict has aggravated an unprecedented humanitarian crisis, especially in Gaza, while simultaneously exposing the erosion of international norms and institutions. The analysis exposes the selective application of international law, the impotence of the Responsibility to Protect (R2P) doctrine, and the failure of institutions like the UN to uphold global justice. The authors critique simplistic frameworks such as Huntington's "Clash of Civilizations", arguing instead for a nuanced understanding of the geopolitical, economic, and humanitarian ramifications of the war.
