title: Genesis of Counterintelligence Activities of Border Authorities and Units of Ukraine

detail.title: Genesis of Counterintelligence Activities of Border Authorities and Units of Ukraine

publicationDetails.detailsText: Naukovij vìsnik Nacìonalʹnoï akademìï vnutrìšnìh sprav, volume 27, issue 2, 2022[10.56215/0122272.87]

detail.abstract: The relevance of the study is conditioned by the investigation and delineation of counterintelligence powers of border authorities and units of Ukraine in different historical periods, determining the areas of their development. The paper is devoted to the study of historical aspects of the development of counterintelligence activities of border agencies, and national and state security bodies on the territory of Ukraine, in particular, the history of transformation of the relevant units and their powers. It is noted that the study of the history of the establishment and functioning of national special services is of practical importance and can become relevant when adjusting the national security strategy. The purpose of the study is to analyse the historical aspects of the development of counterintelligence activities and counterintelligence measures by border authorities and units on the territory of Ukraine in light of retrospective changes in national special services. The methodology of scientific research included a set of interrelated general scientific and historical and legal methods, namely: chronological – to periodise the development of counterintelligence authorities and units of national special services, and the border guard service; comparative legal analysis – a comparative approach to the past and modern legislation, which determines the authority to carry out counterintelligence activities or conduct counterintelligence measures; structural and functional – to classify the threat system, which is carried out by active measures of the main enemy. Features of the legal status of border authorities and divisions of Ukraine in different historical periods are highlighted. It is indicated on the main counterintelligence methods (measures) that were carried out by authorised state bodies and units, namely: the legendary method of capturing prisoners to be interrogated, first mentioned in the annals of the Kievan Rus and conducted mainly during military campaigns; perlustration (interception) of correspondence and external surveillance, their conduct is most characteristic of the period of the Russian occupation; agent measures, during the first liberation competitions, were consolidated in the legal field by the relevant provision, which specifies the main functions of the army special service of the Ukrainian People’s Republic; operational surveillance, legend and operational disinformation (used by both the security service of the organisation of Ukrainian nationalists and Soviet state security agencies). Based on the studies by Ukrainian and foreign researchers, a classification of “active measures” that can be carried out by the aggressor state is presented. The areas of development of the powers of bodies and divisions of the State Border Guard Service of Ukraine to conduct counterintelligence activities are determined.

title: Keep on Trading in the Free World 1

detail.title: Keep on Trading in the Free World 1
detail.abstract: In 2016 the world was rocked by two startling events: the election of Donald Trump in the United States and Brexit in the United Kingdom. While it would be imprudent to put forward simplistic, one-dimensional explanations, both outcomes seem to represent, to some extent, an electoral red card to the 'liberal internationalism' that shaped the world economy over the last decades. On both sides of the Atlantic, many citizens are voicing concerns over the drawbacks of free trade and the globalization process more broadly. This public disquiet is not unprecedented. What is new is how populist candidates used this anxiety with unexpected electoral success. Populist politicians condemn the 'liberal internationalism' that they associate with economic globalization, in particular the promotion of instruments of supranational integration and regulation, trade and investment treaties, etc. (Thompson 2017) Both Brexit and Trump's victory are linked to the conviction that internationally agreed upon rules, multilateralism, and globalization constrain and obstruct national interests (Harris 2016). The electoral emergence of political groups that capitalize on citizens' feelings of economic insecurity has been portrayed as the largest threat to free trade since the Second World War (The Economist 2015). Trump made the protection of domestic interests the hallmark of his Administration, putting an end to a time-honored tradition of American internationalism.

title: Remineralization and Mobilization in the European Southwest Periphery
affiliations: Universidad Pablo de Olavide and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Remineralization and Mobilization in the European Southwest Periphery
detail.abstract: The European energy transition is driving a renewed expansion of mining activities framed as sustainable, strategic, and technologically advanced. This article critically examines this process through the concept of remineralization, defined as the reactivation of extractive frontiers in territories shaped by long-standing pollution legacies, regulatory continuities, and socio-environmental conflict. Drawing on Ecological Economics and political ecology, the paper challenges dominant narratives of “green” mining that portray current extractive expansion as a rupture with past practices.Empirically, the analysis focuses on the European southwest periphery, with particular attention to Andalusia (Spain), a region that has become a testing ground for Europe’s renewed mining agenda. The study is based on twenty-four mining-related conflicts identified through the Map of Mining Environmental Conflicts of Andalusia and Portugal, combining archival research, fieldwork, and conflict mapping. We analyse conflicts by distinguishing structural factors, environmental triggers, and socio-political drivers across multiple spatial and temporal scales. Some relevant cases had their origin during the mining boom under the Franco dictatorship.The findings reveal that accelerated permitting, public-interest exemptions, and green-growth discourses associated with the European Critical Raw Materials Act intensify socio-environmental vulnerability rather than resolve it. At the same time, grassroots mobilizations, legal strategies, and alliances with scientific expertise play a central role in contesting extractivist logics and articulating alternative, post-extractive futures. The article contributes to Ecological Economics by extending debates on extractivism, environmental justice, and valuation conflicts to the European context, highlighting the importance of historical legacies and collective resistance in shaping contemporary mining governance.

title: Local Development Policy Effects on Environmental Quality: The Case of Amathole District Municipality

detail.title: Local Development Policy Effects on Environmental Quality: The Case of Amathole District Municipality

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: Sustainability has become an increasingly significant issue, although practical implementation remains difficult. Pressure from the Constitution’s developmental obligations on local government presents teething problems in South Africa, hampering the transitioning to sustainability especially at sub-national levels, where increased amounts of resources are required to supplement expertise amid negative effects of incoherent efforts and disaggregated planning rendering it difficult to attain minimum levels of sustainability in line with global efforts else. Data gathering on local environmental conditions is haphazard making it impossible for policy makers to have meaningful knowledge of baseline environmental conditions. This study galvanized professionals and academics in the EC province to develop environmental quality indicators, gathering of data on Amathole District’s environmental conditions to conduct an assessment using Multi Criteria Analysis (MCA) with aim to stimulate the municipalities under its legislative authority to implement sustainable policies and comply with national objectives. Pursuant to this endeavour, the state of the environment in the 6 local municipalities of the district evaluated using 25 locally relevant indicators. The values of the indicators have been used to rank the municipalities by multiple criteria analysis (MCA). The results of this comparative approach provide information about the level of sustainability attained in the district as a whole as well as in the individual local municipalities. The objective is for a transparent and objective self-assessment and reporting that will provide the basis for remedial action locally, as recommended by Agenda 21, and the SA National framework on Environmental Sustainability.

title: Predictive Model for Sustainable Exploitation of Geothermal Resources in Africa: The Case of Olkaria Geothermal Field
affiliations: University of Florence, University of Florence, Independent, Independent, Strathmore University and Strathmore University

detail.title: Predictive Model for Sustainable Exploitation of Geothermal Resources in Africa: The Case of Olkaria Geothermal Field

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: The work came out of a collaboration between the various entities through the European project LEAP-RE [H2020 No 963530] (http s://www.leap-re.eu/) specifically under Working Package 9 Geothermal Atlas for Africa (https://www.leap-re.eu/geothermal-atlas4-africa/).

detail.abstract: Geothermal energy is a crucial renewable resource for a sustainable future, especially in African nations cut by the Rift Valley, which holds vast untapped potential. However, high upfront costs and development risks remain key challenges. This study introduces a simplified model calibrated with real data from Kenya's Olkaria geothermal field. The model enables rapid preliminary assessments of both technical and economic performance, requiring minimal input data. Additionally, it incorporates a Life Cycle Assessment to evaluate environmental impacts, an aspect rarely explored in African geothermal studies. The research analyses various technological configurations, including Single Flash, Double Flash, and Organic Rankine Cycle (ORC) systems, aiming to improve efficiency without additional drilling. Findings show that integrating an ORC with existing flash systems can boost energy output by up to 20.1 %, with only a modest rise in the Levelized Cost of Electricity. Compared to the current Olkaria IV setup, hybrid systems demonstrated lower carbon emissions and reduced material resource use per energy output. Results confirm that ORC integration offers the most sustainable pathway for developing high-temperature geothermal resources in the East African Rift. This approach balances energy efficiency, economic feasibility, and environmental impact, providing valuable guidance for future power plant development in regulatory-constrained settings. This work is fully consistent with the objectives of Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) 7 and 13.

title: A Comprehensive Quantitative Evaluation of Global Finance Research: Institutions, Scholars, and Citations
affiliations: Western Kentucky University - Department of Accounting and Finance, Shanghai Business School,  and

detail.title: A Comprehensive Quantitative Evaluation of Global Finance Research: Institutions, Scholars, and Citations

publicationDetails.detailsText: Forthcoming in Review of Quantitative Finance and Accounting

detail.abstract: We conduct a global citation-based assessment of finance research from 28 finance journals published between 1990 and 2024. Our results show a substantial increase in the impact of finance research over time, and highly influential articles are concentrated in leading journals such as the Journal of Finance, Journal of Financial Economics, and Review of Financial Studies. The University of Chicago, Harvard University, New York University, the University of Pennsylvania, and Columbia University are top contributors at the institutional level. For top scholars, Eugene F. Fama, Kenneth R. French, and Andrei Shleifer stand out as the top-three scholars, amassing 3,908.08, 3,208.32, and 2,309.93 weighted normalized citations, respectively. For the total number of articles, Iftekhar Hasan, Frank J. Fabozzi, and Robert W. Faff lead the pack with 136, 126, and 119 articles, respectively. Finally, there is an expanding involvement of emerging economies and non-academic organizations, highlighting the increasing diversity and globalization of finance research.

title: The Macroeconomic Effects of Import Tariffs on the Euro Area: A Model-Based Assessment
affiliations: Bank of Italy, Bank of Italy, Bank of Italy, Bank of Italy and Bank of Italy

detail.title: The Macroeconomic Effects of Import Tariffs on the Euro Area: A Model-Based Assessment

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Italy Occasional Paper No. 960
publicationDetails.journalName: Bank of Italy Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We use a multi-country New Keynesian model of the global economy to assess the macroeconomic effects on the euro area (EA) of an increase in tariffs on U.S. (US) imports, either unilaterally or with retaliatory tariffs by the EA, China (CH) and the rest of the world (RW). Our results are as follows. First, EA output decreases to a larger extent (slightly more than 1% at the trough) under the retaliation scenario than under that of an increase in US tariffs with no retaliation (0.5%). The additional decrease is due to the drop in domestic aggregate demand, only partially offset by the increase in exports to CH. Second, an increase in global trade policy uncertainty reduces aggregate demand and, thus, has recessionary and disinflationary effects on the EA and global economies (EA GDP falls by 1%). We also consider a portfolio rebalancing towards financial assets issued by the EA, CH, the RW. This would induce a depreciation of the US dollar and (modest) expansionary and disinflationary effects on countries other than the US.

title: Synchronization as Manipulation
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Synchronization as Manipulation
detail.abstract: We analyze how coordination manipulation distorts information aggregation in prediction markets. Unlike traditional misinformation, a strategic manipulator exploits traders' sequential awareness structure by releasing synchronized batches of truthful information to create an artificial impression of common knowledge. Modeling a platform that detects such temporal clustering patterns, we characterize a unique equilibrium featuring preemption and show that: (i) undetected coordination creates higher-order adverse selection, expanding bid-ask spreads by a first-order magnitude that is robustly positive across all priors; (ii) a deterrence threshold exists above which manipulation is unprofitable; (iii) increasing detection improves informational efficiency if and only if the residual coordination distortion dominates the informational loss from truthful signals. The model reframes the policy debate from content veracity to timing transparency.

reference: Bank of Italy Occasional Paper No. 961
title: The Effects of Monetary Policy on Gross Domestic Product, Investment and Inflation: An Analysis of Italian Regional Heterogeneity
affiliations: Bank of Italy, Bank of Italy, Bank of Italy and Bank of Italy

detail.title: The Effects of Monetary Policy on Gross Domestic Product, Investment and Inflation: An Analysis of Italian Regional Heterogeneity

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Italy Occasional Paper No. 961
publicationDetails.journalName: Bank of Italy Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper analyzes the impact of the ECB’s monetary policy on Italian regional economies and seeks to identify and explain the heterogeneous effects across regions by focusing on gross domestic product, investment, and inflation. The approach is empirical and involves two stages. First, we estimate impulse response functions at regional level and test for the presence of heterogeneity. Second, we explore the underlying drivers of heterogeneity using synthetic indicators that capture the key structural characteristics of local industrial and banking systems. The analysis uncovers statistically significant heterogeneity. Furthermore, a substantial share of the variance in the responses is explained by differences in the strength of regional industrial structures. The financial fragility of firms and the share of small banks in local credit systems also contribute to explaining the observed heterogeneity, albeit to a lesser extent.

title: A Note on Trade Under Regime Uncertainty
affiliations: Radford University - Department of Economics and Radford University - Department of Economics

detail.title: A Note on Trade Under Regime Uncertainty
detail.abstract: Trade is generally good for economies. This finding permeates economics, though there are still attempts to undermine it. There are stylized game theoretic models that may indicate strategic benefits to tariffs, but even these models do not necessarily address the secondary effects of erratic tariff policies. When tariff policies are difficult to predict, the policy uncertainty creates its own negative pressure on production. This note speaks to the concept that there are more than two players in a trade war.

title: Strategic Autonomy Under Constraint - Dependency Triangle

detail.title: Strategic Autonomy Under Constraint - Dependency Triangle

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial, professional, or personal interests that could be perceived to have influenced the research presented in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is based exclusively on secondary data, publicly available documents, policy reports, and academic literature. It does not involve human participants, patients, personal data, or interventions. Therefore, ethical approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The study was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: Europe's pursuit of strategic autonomy has intensified in response to geopolitical shocks, energy market disruptions and growing concerns over technological sovereignty. While policy initiatives frequently frame these challenges as sector-specific or temporary, this thesis argues that Europe's vulnerabilities in energy, defence and digital infrastructure constitute a structural configuration of dependency that constrains autonomous decision-making even in the absence of explicit coercion.

title: Are Sell-Side Analysts Up to the Challenge of Climate Change?
affiliations: University of Melbourne, University of Melbourne - Department of Finance, University of Oklahoma - Michael F. Price College of Business and University of Oklahoma - Michael F. Price College of Business

detail.title: Are Sell-Side Analysts Up to the Challenge of Climate Change?
detail.abstract: Estimating the financial implications of climate change presents a significant challenge, one that aligns with the specialized expertise of sell-side analysts. This study examines analysts' performance in this context and finds that they exhibit systematic pessimism in their earnings forecasts for carbon-intensive firms. Our results suggest this pessimism is more likely represents a mistake rather than deliberate strategic behavior. Analysts appear to conflate elevated discount rates with diminished earnings prospects. Analysts with prior professional experience in pollutionintensive industries exhibit greater pessimism, suggesting this error is more likely driven by limitations in financial expertise rather than a lack of industry-specific knowledge.

title: When Environmental Policy Backfires: Air Pollution Warnings and Influenza Transmission in South Korea
affiliations: Auburn University

detail.title: When Environmental Policy Backfires: Air Pollution Warnings and Influenza Transmission in South Korea

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no financial or non-financial competing interests to declare.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not require ethics approval as it uses publicly available, de-identified data.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Air pollution warnings aim to protect public health by reducing outdoor exposure, yet they can generate unintended consequences. Using daily province-level panel data from South Korea (2015-2019), this study shows that particulate matter (PM) warnings increase influenza incidence by roughly 10-15 percent, with the largest effects among children and teenagers. The impact emerges gradually and peaks 25-40 days after a warning, consistent with secondary transmission dynamics. Search data indicate a shift toward indoor activities and pollution-related items, supporting a behavioral response that increases indoor congregation. Effects are stronger after the 2017 rollout of Emergency Disaster Texts (EDTs), on business days, and in densely populated, lower-income regions. The increase is concentrated in outpatient cases, suggesting mainly mild to moderate illness. Robustness checks and welfare calculations show that excess flu cases impose substantial additional healthcare costs. Overall, while PM warnings reduce pollution exposure, they may inadvertently raise viral transmission risk by driving people indoors.

title: Disney as a Pedagogical Language
affiliations: Radford University - Department of Economics and Radford University

detail.title: Disney as a Pedagogical Language
detail.abstract: Economics need not live up to its reputation as the "dismal science." This paper explores the use of Disney films as a pedagogical tool to connect foundational economic concepts with students' preexisting cultural knowledge and emotional memories. Drawing on research in teacher language awareness, media-based learning, and episodic memory formation, we argue that the relatability and narrative depth of Disney films make them particularly effective in bridging the gap between everyday language and academic economic discourse. We provide examples of classroom applications-such as using Moana and Frozen to illustrate trade theory, The Little Mermaid for opportunity cost, The Princess and the Frog for entrepreneurship, and Cars for government policy and unintended consequences-demonstrating how film can transform abstract concepts into vivid, memorable lessons. This approach not only seeks to improve comprehension and retention but also to foster curiosity, wonder, and a personal connection to economics that can persist well beyond the classroom.

title: The "need of" Ideal Standards of Everyday Morality for Educational Leaders
affiliations: University of Southeastern Philippines

detail.title: The "need of" Ideal Standards of Everyday Morality for Educational Leaders
detail.abstract: This paper explores the essential role of ethical standards in everyday school leadership, emphasizing the principal’s influence on institutional success and student achievement. Drawing on Karaköse (2009), Lynch (2015), Killian (2010), and Tenuto (2015), this paper highlights the ethical challenges faced by educational leaders and the need for continuous professional development in decision-making. The discussion underscores inclusiveness, shared moral values, and curriculum as central to effective governance. Anchored in the Professional Standards for Educational Leaders (2015), the study argues that servant leadership and clearly defined moral foundations are vital in fostering trust, accountability, and high-quality education. Ultimately, it calls for establishing ideal ethical standards to guide leaders in promoting sustainable school improvement and student success.

affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) - Faculty of Law

detail.title: Huawei v. Conversant: Anti-Suit Injunctions in China – A Response In-Kind to the West

publicationDetails.detailsText: The Chinese University of Hong Kong Faculty of Law Research Paper No. 2026-02
publicationDetails.journalName: The Chinese University of Hong Kong Faculty of Law Research Paper Series

publicationDetails.detailsText: FRAND Cases in Context (Jorge L. Contreras ed., Edward Elgar, 2026)

detail.abstract: In Huawei v. Conversant, the Supreme People’s Court (SPC) of the People’s Republic of China (PRC) issued an act preservation order that has been viewed as the first anti-suit injunction (ASI) in the nation amidst a series of international parallel litigations involving SEP holders and standard implementers. This injunction directed Conversant, an SEP holder, to refrain from enforcing a prior injunction granted by a German court against Huawei, the standard implementer, until the SPC reached a final decision on the fair, reasonable, and nondiscriminatory (FRAND) royalty rate between the parties. This ruling also introduced an innovative “daily fines” measure to ensure the enforcement of the ASI. Subsequent to this landmark ruling, Chinese courts have begun to issue ASIs in other cases related to FRAND disputes.

title: Evolutionary Model of a Token-Based Data Market
affiliations: , School of Economics and Management, Beihang University and University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: Evolutionary Model of a Token-Based Data Market
detail.abstract: Decentralization and digital transformation have aroused growing interest in tokenbased platforms and the design of data markets. We develop a token-based data market model in which data platforms issue utility tokens to price data services, facilitate data exchange, and enhance market e!ciency. Based on the evolutionary game theory, we identify the conditions to achieve an e!cient market equilibrium where all participants actively engage in the data market. We find that tradable tokens enable the spontaneous formation of a secondary market. This market determines the token and data prices at equilibrium, reducing the data platforms' monopoly pricing power and better reflecting other participants' valuations of data. We further demonstrate that token-based data markets exhibit more e!cient and stable equilibrium outcomes compared with the non-tokenized market. This improvement arises because data tokenization functions as a commitment mechanism that integrates market information, network e"ects, and data-related costs into the data valuation process, as ensured by the blockchain-based technical design. Overall, our findings highlight the role of utility tokens as e"ective instruments for payment, coordination, and incentive alignment in data markets. These insights illustrate how token-based platforms can enhance market e!ciency, transparency, and stability, thereby contributing to a more resilient data trading environment.

title: Volatility as an Equilibrium Object

detail.title: Volatility as an Equilibrium Object
detail.abstract: Volatility is the central state variable in modern finance, yet canonical asset-pricing and derivative models treat it as an exogenous primitive-either constant or governed by a latent stochastic process specified outside the economic environment. This paper proposes a different view grounded in foundational research on propagation and amplification: network economies can transform micro shocks into aggregate fluctuations, and financial constraints generate feedback loops that magnify disturbances. We translate these insights into asset pricing by constructing volatility as an equilibrium object pinned down by a fixed point between (i) market tightness (risk-bearing capacity, margins, balance-sheet constraints) and (ii) price fluctuations (return variance). The resulting Endogenous Amplification Volatility (EAV) is a state-dependent volatility input that admits a multiplier form, v EAV (Y) = v exo (Y)/(1-g(Y)), where g(Y) is the loop gain. This representation immediately implies a new priced risk object beyond standard variance risk: amplification risk, i.e. compensation for state transitions that change how shocks map into equilibrium volatility. We derive general asset-pricing implications, including sensitivity explosions as g ↑ 1, volatility regimes and hysteresis under nonlinear feedback, and elevated risk premia in high-gain states. We then establish arbitrage-free valuation results for contingent claims under EAV: European prices satisfy a Feynman-Kac characterization with diffusion scale determined by equilibrium variance, while American prices admit a Snell envelope/obstacle formulation in the augmented state. Finally, we demonstrate operational relevance. European option prices admit a mixture-of-Black-Scholes representation conditional on integrated EAV, and American equity options can be priced efficiently via least-squares Monte Carlo with EAV-adapted state augmentation. We culminate in a practical implementation section that shows how the new theory alters hedging and risk management: we define an amplification Greek, illustrate its impact on American put values and exercise policies, and construct an Amp-neutral overlay portfolio that controls amplification exposure using traded instruments.

title: Intergenerational Mobility in Ottoman Istanbul: Evidence from Court Records
affiliations: University of Connecticut, Yale University and Istanbul Medeniyet University

detail.title: Intergenerational Mobility in Ottoman Istanbul: Evidence from Court Records
detail.abstract: We draw on Istanbul court registers from the 16th-19th centuries to establish long-term trends in intergenerational mobility. The dataset covers more than 270,000 individuals appearing in court in various capacities—litigants, witnesses, representatives, and others—and crucially records honorific titles for both individuals and their fathers. We use these titles as indicators of socioeconomic status. We have three aims. First, we show that honorific titles are reliable proxies for social status in this context. Second, we analyze the relationship between fathers’ and sons’ titles to assess intergenerational mobility. Third, we determine whether any observed shifts reflect horizontal movements within social strata or increased mobility across class boundaries. We find that titles remained strongly and consistently correlated with wealth between the 16th and 19th centuries. During the same period, the intergenerational transmission of titles declined, indicating increased mobility. However, this rising mobility occurred primarily within the elite strata, suggesting a consolidation of power and status among the upper classes rather than a broad opening of the social hierarchy.

title: Digital Sovereignty under Extraterritorial Pressure

detail.title: Digital Sovereignty under Extraterritorial Pressure

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no financial or personal relationships with Kyndryl, Microsoft, Amazon Web Services, or the Dutch institutions analysed (Logius, DNB). This research is an independent policy analysis based on publicly available legal documents, regulatory frameworks (CLOUD Act, GDPR, NIS2 Directive, Schrems II), published investigative journalism (Follow the Money, 2025), and open-source institutional communications. The author declares no conflict of interest.

It does not involve: - Human subjects or research participants - Collection of personal data - Sensitive personal information processing - Interviews with named individuals Consequently, formal ethics approval is not applicable. All analysis is based on public sources, published regulations, and investigative journalism already in the public domain. No confidentiality agreements or restrictions on disclosure apply to the sources analysed.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was conducted independently without external funding. The author received no financial support from governments, foundations, technology providers, or policy institutions for the conduct of this analysis.

detail.abstract: Digital sovereignty is increasingly invoked in European policy debates, yet the term is often diluted into compliance or risk-mitigation language. This paper argues that such dilution obscures the fundamental problem: sovereignty is about exclusive and enforceable control. Where a foreign jurisdiction can exert legal, technical, or economic coercion, sovereignty is structurally absent, even when systems are secure, certified, or hosted in the EU. Two cases are examined. First, the DigiD infrastructure, where a critical layer is operated by Kyndryl, a U.S. "United States person" subject to the CLOUD Act. Even with strong encryption, the combination of metadata exposure and gag orders creates a structural "verification gap": Logius cannot verify whether compelled access has occurred. Second, the DNB case, where the bank warned the financial sector about big-tech dependency but simultaneously deepened its own reliance on Microsoft's cloud services, and discontinued end-to-end encryption. The paper concludes with a detailed risk analysis and a three-phase policy roadmap to restore sovereignty conditions under NIS2, including key-management audits, jurisdiction-aware supply-chain requirements, and credible exit capabilities.

title: The Reckoning: Is 2026 The Beginning Of The End?

detail.title: The Reckoning: Is 2026 The Beginning Of The End?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no conflicts of interest to disclose.
declarations.ethicsApproval: No human subjects were used in this study.
declarations.funderStatement: The author has no external funding or financial conflicts of interest to disclose.
declarations.clinicalTrialRegistration: No clinical trials were conducted in this study.

detail.abstract: The foundations of global stability are quietly unraveling. Not that things were ever perfect, or that this unraveling has not happened before. But the cravings of the great powers and those rising now press against the planet's natural limits. This unraveling is reshaping landscapes, economies, and societies in ways that ripple unpredictably, far more than in previous iterations. At the beginning of this year, 2026, this current affairs analysis consolidates five years of my research and real-world observations. It identifies trends and geopolitical patterns that are increasingly defining the 21st century. This analysis finds fragile institutions straining under pressures they were never built to bear, while populations navigate the uneven fallout of technological acceleration and environmental change. In this tense equilibrium, small decisions carry outsized consequences, and the boundary between order and disruption narrows. Strategic posturing, economic misalignment, and ecological strain no longer operate in isolation; they intertwine, amplifying the fragility of the systems they touch. Therefore, this is not a sudden catastrophe but a slow accretion of tension, a moment when inertia becomes perilous, and restraint appears costly. These conditions create what I call a “forever tipping point” that cascades toward another global war or extensive periods of cross-regional conflicts. It is an unfolding reality that brings humanity to a reckoning. The challenge is not merely to survive, but to cultivate foresight, humility, and renewed cooperation before the cumulative pressures tip the balance irreversibly. In a nuclear epoch, the stakes are now too high, extending beyond nations to the existence of the Earth itself.

title: Semidefinite Programming for Quantum Channel Learning
affiliations: Lomonosov  Moscow State University - Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics, Peter the Great St. Petersburg Polytechnic University, Peter the Great St. Petersburg Polytechnic University, Ioffe Institute, Ioffe Institute and Ioffe Institute

detail.title: Semidefinite Programming for Quantum Channel Learning
detail.abstract: The problem of reconstructing a quantum channel from a sample of classical data is considered. When the total fidelity can be represented as a ratio of two quadratic forms (e.g., in the case of mapping a mixed state to a pure state, projective operators, unitary learning, and others), Semidefinite Programming (SDP) can be applied to solve the fidelity optimization problem with respect to the Choi matrix. A remarkable feature of SDP is that the optimization is convex, which allows the problem to be efficiently solved by a variety of numerical algorithms. We have tested several commercially available SDP solvers, all of which allowed for the reconstruction of quantum channels of different forms. A notable feature is that the Kraus rank of the obtained quantum channel typically comprises less than a few percent of its maximal possible value. This suggests that a relatively small Kraus rank quantum channel is typically sufficient to describe experimentally observed classical data. The theory was also applied to the problem of reconstructing projective operators from data. Finally, we discuss a classical computational model based on quantum channel transformation, performed and calculated on a classical computer, possibly hardware-optimized.

title: Macro Duration: The Internal Memory Network of the Economy

detail.title: Macro Duration: The Internal Memory Network of the Economy
detail.abstract: This paper develops a new theoretical framework that changes the primitive object of persistence analysis from economic variables and frictions to the internal propagation architecture of the economy. Memory is a feature of the economy that allows to retain the imprint of past disturbances even after the original cause has disappeared. It is the economy's capacity to retain the impact of past events through its internal organization. This paper advances a framework in which memory is an architectural property of economic systems, not a property of particular variables, frictions, or microeconomic mechanisms. The economy is treated as a black-box dynamical system and macroeconomic persistence is traced to internal macro architecture. This perspective unifies DSGE models or VARs and also problematic heterogeneous-agent environments within a single conceptual language. Rather than deriving persistence from micro heterogeneity and aggregation, the framework reverses the logic: internal macroeconomic architecture gives rise to macroeconomic persistence-while at the same time micro structures are fully consistent with the same architecture and its outcomes. We no longer need to know who the agents are in order to know whether the economy remembers. Memory capacity is fully characterized at the level of internal propagation architecture. Moreover, I provide explicit mappings from leading macroeconomic frameworks into the memory architecture. I introduce Macro Duration as the economy's intrinsic memory horizon. Macro Duration measures how long past events remain economically relevant in principle. It does not describe how slowly any particular variable adjusts; it describes how persistent the economic system itself is. This perspective opens a fundamentally new margin for economic policy. Policy is no longer only about stabilizing flows or correcting local distortions, but about shaping the economy's internal memory architecture. Financial regulation, market design, industrial policy, and labormarket institutions can be evaluated by how they reconfigure the economy's capacity to store, amplify, or dissipate history. In this sense, policy becomes, in part, the design of economic memory.

title: Six Impossible Things About Finance
affiliations: Systems Forecasting

detail.title: Six Impossible Things About Finance
detail.abstract: In Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass, the White Queen tells Alice she believes "as many as six impossible things before breakfast." This paper asks the reader to similarly entertain six impossible things about finance: that there can be a non-trivial, surprising, and falsifiable prediction about asset price volatility; that the predicted property would have remained unnoticed for over half a century, despite the fact that this has been an area of intense research interest, and there are tens of models of volatility in use; that any such property could have important and previously unnoticed repercussions for things like option pricing; that the property was hinted at all along by a Cheshire-cat like grin; that the property was predicted by a quantum model, despite being unrelated to subatomic particles; and finally that the property could make something else impossible, namely the continuous-time framework that has dominated quantitative finance since the field was invented.

title: India Needs InDIAS as a Dual-Use Instrument for Retirement and Kids' Education
affiliations: Georgetown University - McDonough School of Business

detail.title: India Needs InDIAS as a Dual-Use Instrument for Retirement and Kids' Education
detail.abstract:
India faces a unique set of financial challenges, with citzens having to worry about saving not only for increasingly expensive children's education, but also their own retirement. The private pensions sector remains underdeveloped, resulting in limited access to guaranteed retirement income that can help individuals maintain their pre-retirement standard of living. The same challenges exist for saving for a child's education. 

These challenges demand innovation or as the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) slogan goes: innovation "Zaruri hai". We believe InDIAS (Inflation-linked, Deferred-Income, Annuity-like Securities), if well-designed, could be serve as a dual-use solution to these looming challenges as well as help India finance much-needed infrastructure to foster high economic growth (Viksit Bharat , Atmanirbhar).

title: Tobacco Tariffs in the Colonial Chesapeake
affiliations: Stanford University - Hoover Institution

detail.title: Tobacco Tariffs in the Colonial Chesapeake
detail.abstract: From 1616 through the Revolutionary War (1775-1783), colonial governors and the English Crown levied tariffs on tobacco produced and exported from the colonies of Maryland and Virginia. The colonies imposed export tariffs, and England imposed import tariffs. Tariffs provided revenue for colonial administration and defense and, in its peak year, represented about 7 percent of English tax revenue. In this paper I analyze how export and import tariffs affected the price and volume of tobacco trade between colonial Maryland and Virginia and England, as well as the distribution of the burden of those tariffs. Although the point estimate suggests elastic demand, it is imprecisely estimated. Elasticity-based incidence estimates indicate that approximately 89 percent of the tariff burden was borne by consumers in Europe, allowing the Crown to raise revenue without significantly discouraging colonial production or migration. These estimates illuminate the fiscal constraints faced by the British Crown and provide context on one of the financial incentives for Britain's decision to sustain control of the colonies through the Revolutionary War.

title: LE COOPERATIVE SOCIALI, TRA DATI E NARRAZIONI
affiliations: European Research Institute on Cooperative & Social Enterprises (EURICSE)

detail.title: LE COOPERATIVE SOCIALI, TRA DATI E NARRAZIONI

publicationDetails.journalName: Euricse Working Paper Series

detail.abstract:
ITALIAN: Un'analisi sull'universo delle cooperative sociali italiane restituisce sia conferme, sia l'evidenza di evoluzioni ancora poco studiate. Dopo trent'anni di crescita, il numero di cooperative sociali diminuisce, per effetto principalmente del calo delle nuove costituzioni; aumentano invece le imprese sociali in forma non cooperativa. Il fatturato e l'occupazione complessive invece continuano ad aumentare, ma ad un'analisi disaggregata emerge come vi sia un numero relativamente limitato di cooperative che produce la gran parte del valore economico. La redditività appare molto limitata e, anche in questo caso, il dato aggregato-che permane positivo-è frutto delle performance di una quota residuale di cooperative. Emergono dati inattesi sulla relazione inversa tra redditività e dimensione di impresa. Infine, va evidenziata la notevole crescita delle cooperative ad oggetto plurimo (A+B), dieci anni ampiamente minoritarie e che oggi costituiscono il 40% delle cooperative neo costituite.


ENGLISH: This Working Paper analyses the universe of Italian social cooperatives, providing both confirmation and evidence of evolutions that are still little studied. After thirty years of growth, there has been a decrease in the number of social cooperatives, mainly due to a drop in new formations, while the number of non-cooperative social enterprises has increased. Overall turnover and employment continue to grow; however, a disaggregated analysis reveals that a relatively small number of cooperatives generate most of the economic value. Profitability appears very limited and, again, the positive aggregate figure is attributable to the performance of a residual share of cooperatives. Unexpectedly, an inverse relationship between profitability and enterprise size emerges. Finally, there is the remarkable growth of cooperatives with multiple objects (A+B), which ten years ago were largely in the minority and now represent 40% of newly established cooperatives.

WORKING PAPER WRITTEN IN ITALIAN.

title: LA GOVERNANCE DELLA DOPPIA TRANSIZIONE: UNA RIFLESSIONE SUL MODELLO COOPERATIVO
affiliations: European Research Institute on Cooperative & Social Enterprises (EURICSE), Sapienza University of Rome and University of Trento

detail.title: LA GOVERNANCE DELLA DOPPIA TRANSIZIONE: UNA RIFLESSIONE SUL MODELLO COOPERATIVO

publicationDetails.journalName: Euricse Working Paper Series

detail.abstract:
ITALIAN: La doppia transizione, digitale ed ecologica, rappresenta una delle principali direttrici di sviluppo tracciate dall'agenda politica europea. L'obiettivo è l'accrescimento della competitività dei sistemi produttivi attraverso un migliore (e minor) utilizzo delle risorse naturali (non rinnovabili) che contribuisca a ridurre l'impatto ambientale e gli effetti correlati sul processo di global warming. Il cambiamento dei modelli di produzione e di consumo potrebbe, tuttavia, innescare una serie di ricadute di carattere sociale e culturale e, di conseguenza, indurre nuove situazioni/condizioni di povertà/esclusione. Per tale ragione, risulta di primaria importanza riflettere sulla struttura e le modalità di organizzazione della produzione, in quanto potenzialmente in grado di influenzare le traiettorie innovative dettate dalle trasformazioni in atto (sostenute dalla doppia transizione). A tal riguardo, il presente contributo si concentrerà sul ruolo del modello cooperativo e sugli eventuali rischi associati alla partecipazione alla doppia transizione in termini di maggiore esclusività e quindi rispetto a un possibile indebolimento della sua natura, distintività e sostenibilità.


ENGLISH: The twin transition, digital and ecological, represents one of the main development directions outlined by the European political agenda. The aim is to increase the competitiveness of production systems through a better (and lower) use of natural resources (non-renewable) that contributes to reducing the environmental impact and the related effects on the global warming process. The change in production and consumption models could, however, trigger a series of social and cultural repercussions and, consequently, induce new situations/conditions of poverty/exclusion. For this reason, it is of primary importance to consider and reflect on the structure and ways of organization of production as they are potentially able of significantly influencing the innovative trajectories defined by the ongoing transformations (supported by the twin transition). In this regard, this contribution will deal with the role of the cooperative model and the risks associated with participation in the twin transition in terms of greater exclusivity and, therefore, with respect to a possible weakening of its nature, distinctiveness and sustainability.

title: ICE and the Plenary Power Problem: Extraconstitutional Authority, Budget Incentives, and the Predictable Production of Interior Coercion
affiliations: Liberty University

detail.title: ICE and the Plenary Power Problem: Extraconstitutional Authority, Budget Incentives, and the Predictable Production of Interior Coercion
detail.abstract:
This policy brief argues that the contemporary interior-immigration enforcement model exemplified by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) is structurally illegitimate on constitutional-democratic grounds. The Constitution enumerates a federal power over naturalization, not a general police power over immigration. The modern immigration regime has been constructed through a hybrid of implied powers and sovereignty-based reasoning, and insulated by doctrines often labeled "plenary power." When that exception zone is operationalized as interior coercion-tactical enforcement inside local communities-it predictably generates recurring rights-friction, tail-risk violence, and legitimacy collapse. Building on a political-economy mechanism ("the American Gestapo is a budget line"), the brief formalizes the doctrine→budget→incentives channel and provides a stylized model linking exception strength and accountability to enforcement intensity and tail risk. Using the January 2026 Minneapolis (Minnesota) events as an illustration, the brief motivates an abolition-first replacement architecture: dissolve ICE as constituted, reallocate narrow civil functions into a paper-first administrative compliance system, and route any coercive policing through ordinary criminal-process constraints.

This policy brief is also available at: https://www.eccentricecon.com/p/ice-and-the-plenary-power-problem

title: Robots Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (RUAVs) Toward Multidomain Intelligent Robotic System
affiliations: Universiti Kuala Lumpur Business School

detail.title: Robots Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (RUAVs) Toward Multidomain Intelligent Robotic System

declarations.declarationOfInterest: none
declarations.ethicsApproval: none
declarations.funderStatement: none

detail.abstract: Robots Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (RUAVs) represent a fundamental transformation in the evolution of unmanned systems, moving beyond conventional remotely piloted or semiautonomous drones toward fully intelligent robotic platforms. RUAVs integrate advanced artificial intelligence, autonomous decision-making, adaptive control mechanisms, and multidomain operational capabilities within a unified robotic architecture. Unlike traditional UAVs, RUAVs are capable of perceiving complex environments, learning from real-time data, and independently executing mission-critical decisions under uncertain and high-risk conditions. This theoretical paper develops a conceptual framework for RUAVs, defining their core structural, cognitive, and operational characteristics. The study examines the role of autonomous reasoning systems, energy-adaptive mechanisms, and robotic self-optimization in enabling persistent autonomy across aerial and hybrid operational environments. Emphasis is placed on RUAVs as decision-centric systems rather than platform-centric machines, highlighting their ability to dynamically adapt mission strategies without continuous human intervention. By positioning RUAVs as autonomous robotic agents, this paper contributes to a deeper theoretical understanding of next-generation unmanned aerial technologies. The proposed framework provides strategic and technological insights relevant to future system design, defense and security applications, and the broader development of intelligent robotic aviation systems. The findings aim to support policymakers, engineers, and researchers in anticipating the operational, ethical, and technological implications of RUAV deployment in complex real-world scenarios.

title: Housing Needs and Cooperative Housing Models: A Scoping Review
affiliations: Free University of Bozen-Bolzano and

detail.title: Housing Needs and Cooperative Housing Models: A Scoping Review

publicationDetails.journalName: Euricse Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: The growing affordability crisis has renewed interest in cooperative housing as an alternative to conventional housing. This scoping review explores traditional and emerging cooperative models across Europe, highlighting their potential to address affordability and resident needs. Traditional ownership and rental cooperatives have shown success in delivering affordable housing in different European contexts. Newer models respond to residents' evolving preferences regarding community engagement, social inclusion and sustainable development. The review maps existing research on cooperative housing, identifying key themes, trends, and gaps. It also includes innovative examples of cooperative projects in European cities. Findings stress the role of innovative financing, partnerships with municipalities and the social services sector, and non-speculative land use in sustaining cooperative models. Despite their promise, cooperatives face challenges around inclusivity, financial stability and resident participation. The review concludes with policy recommendations to scale cooperative housing while preserving its core values of social justice and democratic governance.

title: Mapping Platform Cooperatives: Identities, Dimensions and Challenges
affiliations: Scuola Normale Superiore

detail.title: Mapping Platform Cooperatives: Identities, Dimensions and Challenges

publicationDetails.journalName: Euricse Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: Digital solidarity economies have emerged as a response to the dominant platform capitalism of the past three decades. Despite a growing body of scholarship, the identities, dimensions, and challenges faced by platform cooperatives remain poorly understood. Notably, there are no quantitative studies based on a large number of platform cooperatives. This paper presents the first empirically grounded, aggregate mapping of the features of platform cooperatives. It distinguishes between platform cooperativism and platform cooperatives, addressing definitional issues that have emerged since the concept was first introduced. Drawing on the first international economic survey of platform cooperatives, data from 86 businesses across six continents illuminate the identities, dimensions, and challenges of 27 active platform cooperatives. Finally, the paper outlines four major challenges commonly faced by platform cooperatives: legal, financial, governance, and market-related.

title: The Reconstructability Gap: How AI-Generated Narratives Acquire Authority Without Records

detail.title: The Reconstructability Gap: How AI-Generated Narratives Acquire Authority Without Records
detail.abstract: This paper describes a structural property of AI-mediated information systems. Under decision-adjacent conditions, probabilistic systems produce authoritative narrative outputs that influence beliefs and actions while leaving no durable, attributable, or reconstructable record. This creates a reconstructability gap that becomes visible only after reliance has occurred. The phenomenon is independent of domain, correctness, or intent and arises from the interaction between conversational generation, uncertainty compression, and the absence of institutional recordkeeping.

title: Reasoning Without Records: Why AI-Mediated Decisions Require a Ledger

detail.title: Reasoning Without Records: Why AI-Mediated Decisions Require a Ledger
detail.abstract: Most approaches to AI governance focus on outputs: accuracy, bias, explainability, and auditability. These approaches implicitly assume that the informational basis of decisions can be reconstructed after the fact. This paper examines a different limitation. Once AI-mediated reasoning influences belief or action, no durable record of the reasoning state that produced that influence typically exists. We show that conventional logging and audit mechanisms are insufficient because influence arises through multi-turn interaction, narrative compression, and uncertainty collapse rather than isolated responses. We define the concept of a reasoning ledger as a necessary evidentiary object and specify the properties such a ledger must possess to restore reconstructability. This paper does not propose a standard, recommend adoption, or evaluate implementations. Its purpose is to define the class of artifact required, in principle, if AI-mediated reasoning is to remain explainable under later review.

title: Economic Allocation in Wastewater-to-Energy Life Cycle Assessment: Carbon Value and Mitigation Co-benefits of Palm Oil Mill Effluent in the Global South
affiliations: , University of Tokyo, University of Nottingham Malaysia Campus, University of Nottingham Malaysia Campus, University of Nottingham Malaysia Campus, University of Tokyo - Research Center for Advanced Science and Technology (RCAST) and University of Tokyo

detail.title: Economic Allocation in Wastewater-to-Energy Life Cycle Assessment: Carbon Value and Mitigation Co-benefits of Palm Oil Mill Effluent in the Global South

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.

detail.abstract: The valorization of Palm Oil Mill Effluent (POME) into renewable energy transforms a hazardous waste stream into a valuable co-product, introducing complexities in Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) burden partitioning. This study evaluates the environmental profile of POME-generated electricity and investigates how allocation principles influence the carbon intensity of waste-to-energy initiatives in developing economies. A cradle-to-gate LCA was conducted using primary data from four operational biogas plants in Malaysia, with a functional unit of 1 kWh of electricity. Five allocation methods were compared: cut-off, mass, energy, economic allocation, and a modified system expansion approach. Sensitivity analyses were performed to assess the stability of economic allocation against global commodity price volatility. Results indicate that mass allocation assigns a disproportionate upstream burden (72%) to POME, resulting in a prohibitive carbon intensity of 4.57 kgCO₂e/kWh. Conversely, economic allocation attributes only 1.7% of the burden 0.52 kgCO₂e/kWh, better reflecting the waste status of the effluent. Crucially, when accounting for avoided methane emissions, POME-electricity achieves a net negative impact of -3.8 kgCO₂e/kWh. The study concludes that POME-electricity offers superior decarbonization potential through methane avoidance. Economic allocation is identified as the most pragmatic framework for process safety and environmental accounting, as it aligns with financial risk-sharing in real world business ventures. Policymakers are urged to transition toward value-based mechanisms that reward this pollution reduction co-benefit to mobilize private capital for wastewater valorization.

title: Platform Accountability in the Age of AI in India: Reconciling Corporate Autonomy with Digital Human Rights Under the UNGPs Framework
affiliations: University of Lucknow - Faculty of Law

detail.title: Platform Accountability in the Age of AI in India: Reconciling Corporate Autonomy with Digital Human Rights Under the UNGPs Framework

publicationDetails.detailsText: Prashant Kumar Chauhan (2025). Platform Accountability in the Age of AI in India: Reconciling Corporate Autonomy with Digital Human Rights under the UNGPs Framework. Your Voice Magazine, 4(1), 19–22. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18350538

detail.abstract:
The rise of artificial intelligence (AI) in content moderation has transformed digital platforms into powerful gatekeepers of speech, capable of invisibilising dissent and curating information flows without transparency or accountability. In India, this transformation has coincided with an increasingly interventionist regulatory approach, particularly under the Information Technology Rules, 2021. This convergence has led to growing concerns over algorithmic suppression, opaque moderation practices, and the erosion of digital human rights, including freedom of speech and access to information. The central legal dilemma lies in reconciling the operational autonomy of private platforms with the constitutional and international obligations to protect users' rights in the digital realm.

This article critically evaluates India’s current legal framework and its capacity to uphold platform accountability in the AI age. It explores the applicability of the United Nations Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (UNGPs) as a normative blueprint for reform. Drawing on global regulatory models, the article recommends a hybrid approach integrating statutory mandates, soft law mechanisms, algorithmic audits, and independent oversight to ensure that India’s digital governance is both innovation-friendly and rights-respecting.

title: Tax Abatements for Data Centers and Government Output: Short-Run Effects on Public Sector Activity
affiliations: Stanford University - Hoover Institution

detail.title: Tax Abatements for Data Centers and Government Output: Short-Run Effects on Public Sector Activity
detail.abstract: State and local governments use tax abatements to attract data centers, which are capital-intensive facilities with relatively low employment. Prior research on tax incentives has documented positive and negative spillovers depending upon the duration of the firm's tenure, the size of the abatement or subsidy, and the type of firm. This paper estimates the effects of data center location on local government and sector-specific output per capita from attracting data centers through tax abatements. Using a panel dataset of 135 tax abatements granted by 44 counties in 20 states over the past 20 years, I estimate that a tax abatement for a data center led to an increase in government sector output in the year following the incentive. This increase persists into the second year, suggesting modest short-term fiscal changes to the locality. Analysis of county financial data shows no significant increase in tax collections but a marginally significant rise in debt borrowing, indicating that short-run fiscal impacts reflect accommodation costs financed through debt rather than tax base expansion.

title: The Social Courtroom: How a Recursive Arms Race Over Narrative Credibility Forged the Human Mind

detail.title: The Social Courtroom: How a Recursive Arms Race Over Narrative Credibility Forged the Human Mind
detail.abstract: Human evolution presents three interconnected puzzles: sustained encephalization over millions of years, domain-general intelligence unprecedented in nature, and compositional language. We propose that all three emerged from a single ecological condition - Structural Information Asymmetry (SIA) - created when early hominins combined private foraging with delayed, obligatory redistribution at central places. Under SIA, cooperation depended on evaluating post-hoc accounts of unobserved actions, creating persistent selection for both producing credible explanations and detecting deceptive ones. Because these dual functions rely on the same cognitive substrate (episodic reconstruction, causal modeling, counterfactual simulation), improvements in deception directly enhanced detection and vice versa, generating a recursive within-population arms race that prevented evolutionary equilibrium. We show formally that shared-capacity arms races admit parameter regimes that generate sustained directional selection rather than convergence. This dynamic necessarily produces domain-general cognition (to prevent exploitation across knowledge domains) and compositional language (to meet rising credibility thresholds). The framework generates falsifiable predictions, distinguishing it from social complexity, ecological intelligence, and cooperative breeding accounts, providing a tractable basis for empirical tests.

title: Illuminating Crime Prevention: Evidence from Washington, DC's Street Lighting Upgrade
affiliations: University of Connecticut and Georgia Southern University

detail.title: Illuminating Crime Prevention: Evidence from Washington, DC's Street Lighting Upgrade

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: NA
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract:
Research summary: We examine how large-scale investments in urban infrastructure influence crime by evaluating Washington, DC’s 2023 citywide conversion of street lighting to LED technology. Using incident-level crime data from 2014 to 2025 and leveraging the staggered rollout of the upgrade, we estimate its effects using a staggered difference-in-differences design. Our primary analysis uses street segment–month data to capture immediate, micro-level impacts at the locations where lighting was upgraded, complemented by broader community-level effects. The results show significant reductions in nighttime offenses, driven largely by financially motivated crimes and some evidence of decreases in gun-related offenses. The effects persist for at least one year after the intervention. Crime did not reallocate to other times of day, and there is no evidence of displacement into adjacent streets.

Policy implications: These findings provide rigorous evidence that citywide street lighting upgrades, implemented primarily for energy efficiency and service delivery, can yield meaningful public safety benefits. By documenting immediate, dynamic, and spatially diffuse crime reductions, this study advances situational crime prevention and environmental criminology while informing policymakers about the conditions under which investments in the built environment can complement, rather than substitute for, enforcement-based strategies.

reference: A Journey Through European and International Taxation, 2024, 125-136
title: Developing Sustainable Corporate Tax Governance
affiliations: Tilburg Law School

detail.title: Developing Sustainable Corporate Tax Governance

publicationDetails.detailsText: A Journey Through European and International Taxation, 2024, 125-136

detail.abstract:
Taxes and corporations play a notable role in a number of crises the present-day world is facing. The tax behaviour of corporations is closely watched nowadays. The same goes for companies in the ancient Roman world. Many services and functions, such as tax collecting, were privatized.

The corporate executives of the companies grew into a very wealthy management class. This kind of elite enrichment contributed to growing income and wealth (and political power) inequality and ensuing polarization between rich and poor – which contributed to the downfall of the Roman Republic.

Today’s world is changing rapidly and multinational companies are contributing to it. Some corporations are larger than small states, and they influence society and the everyday lives of countless people and the environment in no small measure. But stakeholders such as institutional investors perceive that companies often pay too little attention to their environmental and societal impact. 

In addition, many policy goals that governments pursue and try to achieve through good public governance cannot be achieved without the help of the business community. Sustainable development springs to mind. 
Unsurprisingly, sustainability is also high on many corporations’ agenda and translated into ‘Environmental, Social & Governance’ (ESG) policies. Taxes are crucial to sustainable development. This requires corporations to gear their governance towards sustainability; it requires sustainable corporate tax governance.

This chapter starts with depicting some views on several crises the present-day world is facing. Taxes and corporations play a notable role in each of these crises. A look at Roman history will then show that this is not new to the world. Next various developments in the field of corporate tax governance will be briefly analysed along two dimensions: paying a fair share of taxes and transparency.

title: Making the invisible visible: A reflection method to uncover justice-related design choices in energy models with model developers and users
affiliations: Delft University of Technology - Faculty of Technology, Policy and Management, Delft University of Technology, Delft University of Technology - Faculty of Technology, Policy and Management,  and Independent

detail.title: Making the invisible visible: A reflection method to uncover justice-related design choices in energy models with model developers and users

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethical approval for the workshops was obtained from the relevant ethics committee at TU Delft, and all participants provided informed consent in writing and orally before participation.
declarations.funderStatement: This research is conducted under the NWO-funded JustETrans Project of number KICH1.ED03.20.002. The content of this article does not reflect the official opinion of NWO. Responsibility for the information and views expressed lies entirely with the authors.

detail.abstract: Energy models play a central role in energy transition decisions yet are often treated as objective and value-neutral tools. Increasingly, scholars and practitioners argue that energy justice should be more explicitly linked to energy modelling, both because of its intrinsic importance and in response to contestation of top-down, techno-economic decision-making. Existing efforts largely focus on incorporating justice within model logic, for example through equity metrics or participatory modelling. However, these approaches themselves embed often-implicit assumptions about justice, including who is recognized as a stakeholder, whose knowledge is represented, and which interests are prioritized. Because such choices carry justice implications, it is essential that model developers and users engage reflexively with the modelling process. Yet, few concrete tools exist to support such reflection. This paper asks: How, and to what extent, does a reflection method help model developers and users identify assumptions and choices with potential justice implications? We develop and test a reflection method in two workshops with developers and users of two policyrelevant energy models in the Netherlands: Energy Transition Model and Hestia. Our findings show how structured reflection can surface justice-relevant assumptions across the modelling process. We propose a typology of six ways in which (in)justice can manifest in/via energy models: model scoping, normative assumptions, policy steering effects, errors, complexity, and potential misuse. We identify a persistent "responsibility gap" between modellers and users, whereby responsibility for justice consequences is continually shifted between those who design models and those who apply them. We conclude with implications for integrating reflexivity and justice awareness into energy modelling practice.

reference: In Van Jackson (ed.) Rethinking Insecurity in the Blue Pacific Region. Security in Context Report 24-02. Security in Context (May 2024), pp. 29–37.
title: Fishing, Human Security, and Transboundary Maritime Challenges in the Pacific Islands Region

detail.title: Fishing, Human Security, and Transboundary Maritime Challenges in the Pacific Islands Region

publicationDetails.detailsText: In Van Jackson (ed.) Rethinking Insecurity in the Blue Pacific Region. Security in Context Report 24-02. Security in Context (May 2024), pp. 29–37.

detail.abstract: This article examines how fishing is closely intertwined with human security considerations in the Pacific Islands region in terms of food security, economic security, personal security, community security, and environmental security. Key areas of vulnerability stem from the heavy reliance of these communities on the oceans and the nature of fish stocks as “common-pool resources,” which creates challenges of monitoring and sustainability. As many of the world’s waters increasingly suffer from overfishing and as climate change endangers ocean ecosystems worldwide, these dynamics are gradually impacting the people of the Pacific Islands. Moreover, intensifying threats in neighboring waters from illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing and fisheries crimes such as human trafficking also pose risks to the human security of the region.

title: CBDC Remuneration and the Fragility of Neutrality: A CES Utility Approach
affiliations: and Central University of Finance and Economics

detail.title: CBDC Remuneration and the Fragility of Neutrality: A CES Utility Approach
detail.abstract: We extend the benchmark CBDC model of Abad et al. (2025) by embedding household preferences in a CES utility framework, relaxing the restrictive log-utility assumption and capturing richer substitution patterns between consumption and liquidity services. We demonstrate that universal neutrality no longer holds: only specific variables, like consumption, may remain unaffected, while output, credit, and welfare respond to CBDC introduction. Simulations reveal that welfare critically depends on whether consumption and liquidity are substitutes or complements, highlighting the risk of policy miscalibration and emphasizing the need to empirically estimate substitution elasticities for effective CBDC design.
